[Translator's note: the asterisk appears thus in the source.] You say "رأيت بُوَيْتاتِ العربِ" (I saw the little houses of the Arabs) with the genitive ending, because the final tāʾ is added, since you say "بيوت" and the final tāʾ falls away. And you say "رأيت ذواتِ مال" (I saw women possessed of wealth), because the tāʾ is added; that is because if you paused on the singular you would say "ذاه", but it was joined to "المال" and became a tāʾ which is spoken only with the muḍāf ilayhi (the noun in construct).
His words ﴿هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِن قَبْلُ وَأُتُواْ بِهِ مُتَشَابِهاً﴾: [it is "أُتُوا"] because it has the sense of "جيئوا به" (it was brought to them), not the sense of "أُعْطَوْهُ" (they were given it). As for His words ﴿مُتَشَابِهاً﴾, it does not mean that its parts resembled one another, but that it is alike in excellence, i.e. each one has, of excellence in its kind, the like of what the other has in its kind.

akhfash:26-26.t:
His words ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَسْتَحْى أَنْ﴾: "يستحي" with two yāʾs is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and the Banū Tamīm say "يَسْتَحى" with one yāʾ. The first is the original, because in what has a weak letter in the position of its lām (third radical), they do not weaken its ʿayn (second radical). Do you not see that they said "حَيِيْتُ" and "جَوِيْتُ", and the ʿayn was not weakened? Yet they say "قُلْتُ" and "بِعْتُ", weakening the ʿayn, since the lām was not weak. They only dropped [the yāʾ] because of their frequent use of this word, just as they said "لَمْ يَكُ" and "لَمْ يَكُنْ", "لا أَدْرِ" and "لا أَدْرِي".
He said ﴿مَثَلاً مَّا بَعُوضَةً﴾, because "ما" is redundant (zāʾida) in the speech, and it is really "إنَّ الله لا يستَحي أن يضرِبَ بعوضَةً مَثَلاً" (Allah is not ashamed to strike a gnat as a parable). Some of the Banū Tamīm say ﴿مَثَلاً مَّا بَعُوضَةً﴾ [Translator's note: printed thus in the source; in this reading بعوضةٌ would be nominative], making (ما) like "الذي" (that which) and implying "هو", as though they said "لا يستحي أن يضرب مثلاً الذي هو بعوضةٌ" (He is not ashamed to strike as a parable that which is a gnat), meaning "لا يستحي أن يضرب الذي هو بعوضَةٌ مثلاً".
His words ﴿فَمَا فَوْقَهَا﴾: some said "greater than it", and some said: it is as when you say "فلان صَغِير" (so-and-so is small) and [another] says "وفوقَ ذلك" (and above that), meaning "وأصغَرُ * من ذلك" (and smaller than that). [Translator's note: the asterisk appears thus in the source.]
His words ﴿مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَـٰذَا مَثَلاً﴾: "ذا" may be like "الذي". And "ماذا" may, if you wish, be a single noun, like "ما", as He said ﴿مَاذَا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُواْ خَيْراً﴾: if "ذا" were like "الذي", they would have said "خيرٌ", and the nominative would be the proper way of the speech. Yet the accusative is permissible in it, because if he said "ما الذي قلت؟" (what is it that you said?) and you said "خيراً", i.e. "قلت خيراً" (I said good), it would be permissible. And if you said "ما قلت؟" (what did you say?) and he said "خيرٌ", i.e. "الذي قلت خيرٌ" (what I said is good), it would be permissible, except that it does not follow the wording of the first [question], as some Arabs, when asked "كيف أصبحت؟" (how are you this morning?), say "صالحٌ" (well), i.e. "أنا صالحٌ" (I am well). What shows you that "ماذا" is a single noun is the poet's saying [in the wāfir metre; this is the thirtieth evidentiary verse]:
دَعِي ماذا علمتُ سأَتَّقيهِ * ولكنْ بالمغيَّبِ نَبِّئِيني
(Leave what I know — I shall guard against it; but tell me of what is hidden.)
If "ذا" here had the sense of (الذي), it would not be [proper] speech.

akhfash:27-27.t:
As for His words ﴿عَهْدَ ٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِ أَن يُوصَلَ﴾: "أَنْ يُوصل" is a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ in "به", like your saying "مررت بالقومِ بعضِهم" (I passed by the people, some of them).
As for "ميثاقه", it has come in place of "التَوثُّق" (making firm), as He said ﴿أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ نَبَاتاً﴾, the original being "إِنباتاً", and as he said "العَطاء" in place of "الإِعطاء" (giving).

akhfash:28-28.t: His words ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتاً فَأَحْيَاكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾: He is only saying "you were dust and drops of sperm", and that is dead. This is acceptable in the speech of the Arabs: you say of a garment "قَدْ كان هذا قُطْنا" (this was cotton), and "كان هذا الرُّطَبُ بُسْرا"* (these ripe dates were unripe dates). [Translator's note: the asterisk appears thus in the source.] Similar to that is your saying to a man "اعمل هذا الثوب" (make this garment) when you have only yarn with you.

akhfash:29-29.t:
This is a chapter on figurative usage (majāz).
As for His words ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّاهُنَّ﴾, while He mentioned only one heaven: this is because the mention of "السماء" (the sky/heaven) has indicated all of them. Some of the exegetes claimed that "السماء" is a collective, like "اللبن" (bricks). What has the wording of a singular and the meaning of a plural may be treated as plural, so He said ﴿سَوّاهُنَّ﴾. Some of them claimed that His words ﴿السَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾ are a masculine collective like "اللّبن". We have not heard this from the Arabs; the first explanation is good.
Yūnus said: ﴿السَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾ is made masculine, as some feminines are made masculine, as the poet said [in the mutaqārib metre; this is the thirty-first evidentiary verse]:
فلا مُزْنَةٌ وَدَقَتْ وَدْقَها * ولا أرضُ** أبقلَ إبقالَها
(No rain-cloud poured down its rain [like it], and no land brought forth herbage like its herbage.)
[Translator's note: the double asterisk appears thus in the source.]
And his saying [in the mutaqārib metre; this is the thirty-second evidentiary verse]:
فإمّا تَرَيْ لِمَّتى بُدِّلَتْ * فإنَّ الحوادِثَ أَوْدَى بِها
(If you see that my locks have been changed — the vicissitudes [of time] have destroyed them.)
"السماء" may be used meaning the plural, as you say "هَلَكَ الشاةُ والبعيرُ" (the sheep and the camel perished), meaning every camel and every sheep, and as He said ﴿خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ﴾, i.e. of the earths.
As for His words ﴿اسْتَوى إلى السمآء﴾, that was not from Allah the Blessed and Exalted by way of moving; rather it means His act, as you say "كان الخَلِيفَة في أهْلِ العراق يوليهم ثم تحوّل إلى أَهلِ الشام" (the caliph was with the people of Iraq, appointing [governors] over them, then he turned to the people of Syria): you only mean that his activity turned.

akhfash:74-74.t:
He said ﴿فَهِيَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً﴾: His saying ﴿أَوْ أَشَدُّ﴾ is not like your saying "هُوَ زيدٌ أو عمرو" ("he is Zayd or ʿAmr"); this is only the ﴿أَوْ﴾ that has the meaning of the wāw, as in your saying "نَحْنُ نأكُل البُرَّ أَوْ الشَعير أو الأُرُزَّ، كلَّ هذا نَأْكُلُ" ("we eat wheat or barley or rice — all of this we eat"). So ﴿أَشَدُّ﴾ is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject); it is only "and they are harder". Some of them said ﴿فَهْيَ كالحِجارَةِ﴾, giving the hāʾ sukūn, and some of them give it a kasra. That is because the usage of the Arabs with "هيَ", "هَو" and the lām of command, when a wāw or fāʾ precedes them, is to give their first letters sukūn; and some of them leave them [vowelled]. He said ﴿وَهُوَ ٱللَّهُ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ﴾ [and] He said ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾. [And] He said ﴿وَلْيتوبوا﴾ — [one] pausing [before it] and using the kasra. And He said ﴿فَلْيَعْبُدُواْ﴾ — pausing and using the kasra.
Chapter on إِنَّ and أَنَّ.
He said ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلأَنْهَارُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَآءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ﴾: this lām is the lām of emphasis (tawkīd), and it has a fatḥa; it falls on the noun on which "إنَّ" falls when there is an intervening element between it and "إِنَّ", like this. [And] it is like "إنَّ في الدارِ لَزَيْداً" ("in the house is indeed Zayd"). It also falls in the khabar of "إنَّ", and it turns "إِنَّ" to the inceptive [kasra form]: you say "أَشْهَدُ إنَّهُ لَظَريفٌ" ("I testify that he is indeed charming"). Allah the Mighty and Majestic said ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ وَٱللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾, and He said ﴿أَفَلاَ يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي ٱلْقُبُورِ [9] وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ إِنَّ رَبَّهُم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّخَبِيرٌ﴾. If there were no lām in this, it would be "أَنَّ رَبَّهُمْ", because heavy "أنَّ", when it together with what it governs stands in the place of "ذاكَ" ("that") or in the place of a noun, is always "أَنَّ" with a fatḥa; and if a noun would not be good in the place of it and what it governs, then it is "إنَّ" as an inceptive. Do you not see His saying ﴿ٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَتِي ٱلَّتِيۤ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾? He is saying "remember this". And He said ﴿فَلَوْلاَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَبِّحِينَ لَلَبِثَ﴾, because "لولا ذاكَ" ("were it not for that") is good in its place. Everything in which it is good to put "ذاك" in place of "أنَّ" and what it governs is "أَنَّ". But when you say ﴿يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ﴾, it would not be good to say "يَعْلَم لَذالِكَ". If you say: "Drop the lām as well and say 'يُعْلَمُ ذَاكَ'", [the answer is that] the lām is not among what "إِنّ" governs. As for His saying ﴿إِلاَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ﴾, this did not take the kasra because of the lām; [and] if the lām were not in it, it would still be "إنَّ", because it is not good to say "ما أَرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ إلاّ ذَاكَ" ("We did not send before you except that"), "ذاكَ" being the story. The poet said [in the munsariḥ metre; it is the eighty-ninth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
ما أَعْطيانِي وَلا سَألْتُهُما * إلاّ وإني لَحاجِزِي كَرَمي
(They did not give to me, nor did I ask them, except that my nobility was indeed restraining me.)
If the lām were dropped from this too, it would be "أَن" [Translator's note: printed thus; by the argument just made, the expected form is «إنّ»; translated as written]. And He said ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾, as though He said "that is the matter"; and this — His saying ﴿وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾ — "هذا" ("this") can stand in its place. And He said ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾, as though in answer to someone who said "What is the matter?" or the like, so He says to those asking: "That is …", as though He said "That is the matter, and that Allah weakens the plot of the disbelievers"; so it is good to say "ذلكم" and "هذا". You imply the khabar, or make it the khabar of an implied [mubtadaʾ]. And He said ﴿إِنَّ لَكَ أَلاَّ تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلاَ تَعْرَىٰ﴾ ﴿وَأَنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا وَلاَ تَضْحَىٰ﴾, because it is permissible to say "إنَّ لَكَ ذاكَ" and "هذا"; and in these three words the kasra of "إِنَّ" as an inceptive is permissible. ﴿فَنَادَتْهُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ . . أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ﴾: it is permissible to say "the angels called him with that"; and if you wish, you may put it in the nominative [i.e. the inceptive form] as reported speech (ḥikāya), as though He said "the angels called him and said: 'إِنَّ اللّهُ يُبَشِّرُكَ'", because everything after [the verb of] saying is reported speech: you say "قُلْتُ: عبدُ اللّهِ مُنْطَلِقٌ" ("I said: ʿAbd Allāh is leaving") and "قلت: إنَّ عبدَ اللّهِ زيداً مُنْطَلِقٌ" [Translator's note: printed thus, with «زيداً» apparently intrusive], except in the dialect of those Arabs who make [the verb of] saying govern like [the verb of] thinking; for such a one it is proper to give "أَنَّ" the fatḥa. And He said ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾, and they claim that this is "ولأنَّ هذهِ أمَّتَكُم أُمَّةٌ واحدةٌ وَأَنَا رَبُّكُّمْ فَاتَّقُونِ", He is saying "so fear Me, because this is your community", and this is good in it likewise. If you say, "How can the lām be supplied when it was not in the speech?", [the answer is that] dropping the lām and similar prepositions from "أَنَّ" is good; do you not see him saying "أَشْهد أَنَّك صادِقٌ" ("I testify that you are truthful"), while it is only "I testify to that"? And He said ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱلْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلاَ تَدْعُواْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾, saying "so do not call upon anyone with Allah, because the mosques belong to Allah". In this parsing there is weakness, because what comes after it governs it, attaching it to itself by a preposition; if you said "أنّكَ صالِحٌ بَلَغَنِي" ("that you are righteous reached me") it would not be permissible, even though it is permissible in that [other case], because when the preposition comes first, its implication is strong. It has also been read with the kasra. Some of them said: "This is only [conjoined] to ﴿أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ﴾, and 'it has been revealed to me that the mosques belong to Allah', and 'it has been revealed to me that when the servant of Allah stood'". And ﴿وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا﴾ has been read [with the fatḥa], so the fatḥa of every "أَنْ" in it is permissible on [the basis of] the revelation.
And some of them said ﴿وَإِنَّهُ تَعالى جَدُّ رَبِّنا﴾, giving it the kasra as part of the speech of the jinn: since it came after [the verb of] saying, it became reported speech, and likewise what follows it of the speech of the jinn.
As for "إنَّما": when "أَنَّ" is good in its place, you give it the fatḥa, and when it is not good, you give it the kasra. He said ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنَاْ بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمْ إِلَـٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾: in the second one "أَنَّ" is good in its place, so you say "it is revealed to me that your God is one God". The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the ninetieth shāhid]:
أرانِي - وَلا كُفْرانَ لِلّهِ - إنَّما * أُواخِي من الأقْوامِ كُلَّ بَخِيلِ
(I see myself — and no ingratitude to Allah — befriending among the tribes only every miser.)
Because "أَنَّ" is not good here: [so] if you said "أَراني أنما أواخي من الأقْوام", it would not be good. And he said [in the khafīf metre; it is the ninety-first shāhid]:
أَبْلِغ الحارثَ بنَ ظالِمِ المُو * عِدِ والناذِرَ النُّذُورَ عَلَيّا
أَنَّما تَقْتُلُ النِّيامَ، وَلا تَقْـ * ـتُلُ يَقْظانَ ذا سِلاحٍ كَمِيّا
(Convey to al-Ḥārith ibn Ẓālim, the one who threatens and makes vows against me, that you only kill sleepers, and do not kill one awake, armed and clad in armour.)
So it is good to say "that you kill the sleepers". As for the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتٌّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ﴾, the second is a badal (substitute) for the first.
As for light "إنْ", it may have the meaning of "ما" (negation), as in the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿إِنِ ٱلْكَافِرُونَ إِلاَّ فِي غُرُورٍ﴾, i.e. "the disbelievers are not". And He said ﴿إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَلَدٌ﴾, i.e. the Most Merciful has no son, ﴿فَأَنَاْ أَوَّلُ ٱلْعَابِدِينَ﴾ — of this community — to the Most Merciful, by denying a son to Him.
I.e. I am the first of the worshippers [in affirming] that the Most Merciful has no son. And some of them said ﴿فَأَنا أَوَّلُ العَبِدِين﴾, saying: "I am the first to be angered by your claiming a son for Allah".
And one says "عَبِدَ", "يَعْبَدُ", "عَبَدا", i.e. he became angry. And He said ﴿وَتَظُنُّونَ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾: it always has the kasra when it has the meaning of "ما". Likewise ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَاهُمْ فِيمَآ إِن مَّكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ﴾: "إنْ" is in the place of "ما", and the "ما" before it is in the place of "الذي". It may also be for the conditional, as in His saying ﴿وَإِن تُبْدُواْ مَا فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ﴾ and ﴿وَإِن تَعْفُواْ وَتَصْفَحُواْ﴾. And "إنْ" is added [as redundant, zāʾida] with "ما": they say "ما إنْ كانَ كَذا وَكَذا", i.e. "it was not such-and-such", and "ما إنْ هذا زَيْدٌ" ("this is not Zayd"). But it alters "ما", so that the khabar is not put in the accusative by it. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; it is the ninety-second shāhid]:
وما إنْ طِبْنا جُبْنٌ وَلَكِنْ * مَنايانا وَطُعْمَةُ آخَرِينا
(Our custom is not cowardice; rather, [it was] our fated deaths and the good fortune of others.)
And it may be light with the meaning of the heavy one, having the kasra, and it only occurs with the lām in its khabar: they say "إنْ زَيْدٌ لَمنطلِقٌ" ("Zayd is indeed leaving"), and they do not say it without the lām for fear that it be confused with the one whose meaning is "ما". They have claimed that some of them say "إنْ زيداً لمَنطَلِقٌ", making it govern according to the meaning. It is like ﴿إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ﴾, which is read with the accusative and the nominative; and "ما" is added for emphasis, and the lām is added for emphasis. It is the one in His saying ﴿وَإِن كَانَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأَيْكَةِ لَظَالِمِينَ﴾; but it fell on the verb only when it was lightened, just as "لكنْ" falls on the verb when it is lightened. Do you not see that you say "لكن قد قال ذاك زيد" ("but Zayd has said that")? And they did not strip it of the lām in His saying ﴿وَإِن كَانَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأَيْكَةِ لَظَالِمِينَ﴾. On this dialect, as we see it — and Allah knows best — is ﴿إِنْ هَـٰذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ﴾. Some people pronounced it heavy, saying ﴿إنّ هذانِ﴾, and this is hardly known, except that they claim that the Balḥārith ibn Kaʿb make the yāʾ in things like this an alif, saying "رأيت أخواك" ("I saw your two brothers") and "رأيت الرجلان", "وضعته علاه" ("I put it on him") and "ذهبت إلاهُ" ("I went to him"); so they claimed that it is read with the heavy form according to this dialect. Abū Zayd claimed that he heard an eloquent Bedouin of the Balḥārith say "ضَرَبْتُ يَداهُ" ("I struck his two hands") and "وضعته علاه", meaning "يدَيْه" and "عَلَيهِ". And some of them said ﴿إنَّ هذَيْنِ لَساحِران﴾, and that is contrary to the written text [of the Muṣḥaf]. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; it is the ninety-third shāhid]:
طاروا عليهن فَشُلٌ عَلاها * واشْدُدُ بمثْنى حَقبٍ حَقْواها
ناجَيَةً وناجِياً أَباها.
(They leapt onto them [the camels], so go up on her and fasten tight her two flanks with a doubled girth-strap — a swift she-camel, and swift was her sire.)
As for light "أَنْ", it may be redundant with "فَلمَّا" and "لَمّا": He said ﴿فَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَ ٱلْبَشِيرُ﴾, and it is only "when the bearer of good news came"; and He said ﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا﴾, saying "and when [they] came". It is also added with "لَوْ": they say "أَنْ لَوْ جِئْتني كانَ خيراً لك" ("if you had come to me it would have been better for you"), meaning "لَوْ جِئْتَني". And it may have the meaning of "أَي" ("that is"): He said ﴿وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلْمَلأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ ٱمْشُواْ﴾, saying "that is: walk on". And it may be light with the meaning of the heavy one, as in His saying ﴿أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ﴾ and ﴿أَنَّ لَعْنَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ [Translator's note: the second phrase is printed here with heavy «أَنَّ», although the discussion is of the light form], on [the basis of] your saying "أَنْهُ لَعْنَةُ اللّهِ" and "أَنْهُ الحَمْدُ لِلّهِ". And this is in the position of His saying ﴿أَفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلاً﴾ [and] ﴿وَحَسِبُوۤاْ أَلاَّ تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾. But when this is lightened and is next to the verb, it is not good unless "لا" is with it, so that it compensates for the loss of the heaviness and of the implied [pronoun]. "لا" does not compensate in His saying ﴿أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ﴾, because, being light, it does not govern the noun; and they compensated it with "لا" when it was with the verb, because they wanted to make clear that it does not govern in this place and that it is heavy in meaning. And light "أنْ" may govern the verb, and it together with the verb is a noun for the maṣdar (verbal noun), as in His saying ﴿عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ﴾: it is only "[able] to restoring his fingertips".

akhfash:78-78.t:
Chapter on exception.
﴿وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْكِتَابَ إِلاَّ أَمَانِيَّ﴾ is accusative because it is an excepted [noun] that is not of the [category of the] first part of the speech. This is the one that comes in the meaning of "لكن" ("but"), standing outside the first part of the speech; He only means "but wishful fancies" and "but they wish". We have explained it by "لكن" only to make clear its being outside the first [part]. Do you not see that when you mention "لكن", you find the speech cut off from its beginning? There is much like that in the Quran, [among it the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic] ﴿وَمَا لأَحَدٍ عِندَهُ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰ﴾ ﴿إِلاَّ ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ﴾, and He said ﴿مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلاَّ ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ﴾, and He said ﴿فَلَوْلاَ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ أُوْلُواْ بَقِيَّةٍ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْفَسَادِ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾, saying "why was there not among them someone who would forbid", then He said "but a few of them are those who forbid", then He said "but a few of them did forbid"; so when it came as an excepted [noun] outside the first [part], it was accusative. Like it is ﴿فَلَوْلاَ كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَآ إِيمَانُهَا إِلاَّ قَوْمَ يُونُسَ﴾: He says "why was there not", then He said "but the people of Jonah". So "إلا" comes in the meaning of "لكنّ"; and when you know that it is in the meaning of "لكنّ", you ought to recognise its being outside its beginning. And ﴿إِلاَّ قَوْمُ يُونُسَ﴾ may be nominative, with "إلاّ" and what follows it in the position of an attribute, in the place of "غير" ("other than"), as though He said "why was there not a town that believed, other than the town of the people of Jonah". Like it is ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ آلِهَةٌ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾: His saying ﴿إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾ is an attribute; [and] were it not for that, it would be accusative, because it is an excepted [noun] placed first that may be dropped from the speech, and every excepted [noun] placed first that may be dropped from the speech is accusative. And this may be dropped: [so] if you said "were there gods in them both, they would both have been ruined", it would be permissible. So the accusative is permissible in it, and it would be like his saying "ما مَرَّ بي أحَدٌ إلاَّ زيداً مثلُكَ" ("no one like you passed by me except Zayd"). The poet said, regarding what is an attribute [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the ninety-fourth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
أُنِيخَتْ فألقتْ بَلْدَةً فَوْقَ بَلْدَةٍ * قَليلٌ بها الأَصْواتُ إلاَّ بُغامُها
(She was made to kneel, and she laid her chest upon a land in which voices are few, other than her own soft groaning.)
And he said [in the wāfir metre; it is the ninety-fifth shāhid]:
وَكُلُّ أخٍ مُفارِقُهُ أَخُوه * لَعَمْرُ إِبيكَ إلا الفَرْقَدانِ
(And every brother will be parted from by his brother — by your father's life — other than the two Farqad stars.)
Like the accusative that is in the meaning of "لكنْ" is the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَإِن نَّشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلاَ صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يُنقَذُونَ﴾ ﴿إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً مِّنَّا﴾; and it is frequent in poetry and in speech. Al-Farazdaq said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the ninety-sixth shāhid]:
وما سَجَنُوني غيرَ أَني ابْنُ غالِبِ * وأَني من الأَثرَينَ غَيْرَ الزَعانِفِ
(They did not imprison me, except that I am the son of Ghālib, and that I am of the most numerous, not of the hangers-on.)
He is saying "but I am". It is like their saying "ما فيها أحدٌ إلا حماراً" ("there is no one in it except a donkey"): since it was not of [the category of] the first part of the speech, it was put on the meaning of "لكنَّ". And like it is [in the khafīf metre; it is the ninety-seventh shāhid]:
ليسَ بَيْنِي وبينَ قيسٍ عِتابَ * غيرَ طَعْنِ الكُلا وَضَرْبِ الرِقابِ
(Between me and Qays there is no reproach other than piercing kidneys and striking necks.)
And his saying [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the ninety-eighth shāhid]:
حَلَفْتُ يميناً غَير ذِي مَثْنَوِيَّةٍ * وَلا عِلْمَ إلاَّ حُسْنَ ظَنٍّ بِغَايِبِ
وبصاحب.
(I swore an oath without reservation, and [I have] no knowledge, only a good opinion of one absent — and of a companion.)
Chapter on the plural.
As for the doubling of [the yāʾ in] ﴿ٱلأَمَانِيُّ﴾, it is because its singular, "أُمْنِيَّة", is doubled; and everything whose singular is doubled, like "بُخْتِيَّة" (Bactrian she-camel) and "بَخاتِيّ", is doubled. Some of them read ﴿إلاّ أَمانِي﴾, lightening it, and that is permissible, because the plural is not [formed exactly] on its singular: [letters] are taken away from it and added to it. As for "الأَثافِي" (the hearthstones), all of them lighten it, while its singular, "أُثِفيَّة", is doubled; they only lightened it because they use it often in speech and poetry, and its doubling is permissible by analogy. Like the lightening of "الأمانِي" is their saying "مِفْتاح" and "مَفاتِح", and for "مِعْطاء", "مَعاطٍ". Al-Akhfash said: "I have heard the Balʿanbar say 'صحارِيَ' and 'مَعاطِيّ', doubling [the yāʾ]."
And His saying ﴿وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَظُنُّونَ﴾, i.e. "they do nothing but conjecture".

akhfash:235-235.t:
He said: ﴿وَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾. "الخِطْبَةِ" is the mention [of marriage], and "الخُطْبَةَ" is the tashahhud [formal address].
And He said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرّاً﴾, because when He said ﴿لاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ it was as though He had said "you mention [it]"; ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرّاً إِلاَّ أَن تَقُولُواْ﴾ is an exception falling outside [the first statement], on [the meaning of] "but" ("ولكنْ").

akhfash:237-237.t:
He said: ﴿فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ﴾, that is: then upon you is half of what you specified, ﴿إِلاَّ أَنْ يَعْفُونَ﴾. If you wish you may put ﴿نصفَ ما فَرضْتُمْ﴾ in the accusative, as a command.
And He said: ﴿وَأَن تَعْفُوۤاْ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ وَلاَ تَنسَوُاْ ٱلْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾. Some read ﴿ولا تَناسَوْا﴾, and all are correct. Some read ﴿وَلا تَنْسَوِا الفَضْلَ﴾, giving the wāw kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as He said ﴿ٱشْتَرُواْ ٱلضَّلاَلَةَ﴾.

akhfash:239-239.t: He said: ﴿فَإنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجَالاً أَوْ رُكْبَاناً﴾. He is saying: "pray on foot or pray riding".

akhfash:240-240.t: He said: ﴿وَصِيَّةً لأَزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾, as though [He said]: "for their wives there is a bequest" ﴿مَّتَاعاً إِلَى ٱلْحَوْلِ﴾. He put ﴿مَتاعاً﴾ in the accusative because, when He said ﴿لأزْواجِهِمْ﴾ ﴿وَصِيَّةً﴾, it was as though He had said: "so provide for them" ﴿مَتاعاً﴾ (a provision). On this basis His saying ﴿مَّتَاعاً إِلَى ٱلْحَوْلِ غَيْرَ إِخْرَاجٍ ﴾ is accusative. He is saying "not an expulsion", that is: "a provision, not an expulsion", that is: do not expel them at all. They claimed that in the reading (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd it is ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيكُم وَصِيَّةٌ لأزْواجِكم﴾.

akhfash:241-241.t:
He said: ﴿وَلِلْمُطَلَّقَاتِ مَتَاعٌ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ حَقّاً﴾, that is: I make that a duty, as a duty.
Some read ﴿وَصِيَّةٌ لأَزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾ (240) — he put it in the accusative as a command [and in the nominative], that is: "upon you is a bequest of that" [and] "make a bequest for them". [Translator's note: the passage as written is muddled: the quoted form has the nominative وَصِيَّةٌ; the explanation "upon you is a bequest" fits the nominative and "make a bequest" fits the accusative.]

akhfash:245-245.t:
He said: ﴿مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً فَيُضَاعِفَهُ لَهُ﴾. Some read ﴿فَيُضَعِّفُه لَهُ﴾. It is also read in the accusative, if you intend the first to be a noun, because a verb cannot be conjoined to a noun; so in His saying ﴿فيُضاعِفَهَ﴾ "أنْ" is implied so that it becomes a noun, and you make it follow the first when the noun is intended by it. The nominative is the dialect of Banū Tamīm, because they do not intend the first to be a noun, and so they conjoin a verb to a verb. His saying ﴿يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ﴾ is not because of any need on Allah's part; rather, it is like the Arabs' saying "لكَ عِنْدي قرضُ صِدْقٍ" ("you have a true loan with me") and "قَرْضُ سَوءٍ" ("a bad loan"), for something in which one's pleasure or displeasure comes. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the one hundred and forty-sixth shāhid (attested verse)]:
لا تَخْلِطَنَّ خَبيثاتٍ بِطَيِّبَةٍ * واخْلَعْ ثيابك مِنْها وانجُ عُرْيانا
كُلُّ امرِىءٍ سوفَ يُجْزى قرضَهُ حَسَناً * أوْ سَيِّئاً أَوْ مَدِينا مثلَ ما دانا
(Do not mix foul deeds with a good one; strip your garments of them and escape naked. Every man will be repaid his loan, good or bad, or be requited just as he requited.)
So "القَرْض" is whatever good or bad has gone before.

akhfash:246-246.t:
He said: ﴿وَمَا لَنَآ أَلاَّ نُقَاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ﴾. ﴿أنْ﴾ here is redundant (zāʾida), just as it is added after "فلما", "لَما" and "لَوْ"; it is added in this sense frequently. Its meaning is "and why should we not fight?"; yet He let "أَنْ" govern, though it is redundant, just as one says "ما أَتاني منْ أحَدٍ" ("no one came to me") and lets "مِنْ" govern, though it is redundant. Al-Farazdaq said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the one hundred and forty-seventh shāhid]:
لَوْ لَمْ تَكُن غَطَفانٌ لا ذُنُوب لَها * إليَّ لامَتْ ذَوو أَحْسابِها عُمَرَا
(Had Ghaṭafān not had sins against me, the men of standing among them would have blamed ʿUmar.)
The meaning is: had Ghaṭafān not had sins. "لا" is redundant, and he let it govern.

akhfash:248-248.t: He said: ﴿فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾. "السَّكِينَةُ" is gravity and calm. As for the iron [blade], it is "السِّكِّينُ" (the knife), with the kāf doubled. Some said: "هي السِّكِّينُ", like it in the doubling except that it is feminine, so he made it feminine; the feminine is not the well-known usage. Banū Qushayr say "سِخِّين" for the knife. And He said ﴿وَآتَتْ كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِّنْهُنَّ سِكِّيناً﴾.

akhfash:251-251.t: He said: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾. You put ﴿ٱلنَّاسَ﴾ in the accusative because you make the action fall upon them, then you made ﴿بَعْضَهُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) of them for explanation.

akhfash:253-253.t:
He said: ﴿مِّنْهُمْ مَّن كَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ﴾, that is: Allah spoke to him; [the word "Allah"] in this place is nominative.
And He said: ﴿وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٍ﴾, that is: Allah raised some of them in degrees.

akhfash:255-255.t:
He said: ﴿لاَ تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلاَ نَوْمٌ﴾. You say "وسِنُ", "يوسَنُ", "سِنَّة" and "وَسَناً" (to doze, drowsiness). [Translator's note: so in the text; the usual forms are وَسِنَ، يَوْسَنُ، سِنَةً.]
And He said: ﴿وَلاَ يَؤُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا﴾, because it is from "آدُه", "يَؤُودُهُ", "أَوْداً"; its explanation is: it does not burden Him.

akhfash:256-256.t: He said: ﴿قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَيِّ﴾, and if you wish ﴿الرَّشَدُ من الغَيِّ﴾ — with ḍamma and with fatḥa.

akhfash:257-257.t:
[He said]: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَوْلِيَآؤُهُمُ ٱلطَّاغُوتُ﴾: it is plural in meaning and singular in form; it has been pluralised, and they said "الطَواغيتُ".
As for His saying ﴿يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ﴾, He is saying: "He judges that they are thus", just as you say "قَدْ أَخْرَجُك الله من ذا الأمر" ("Allah has taken you out of this affair") when you were never in it; and you say "أَخْرَجَنِي فُلانُ من الكِتْبَةِ" ("So-and-so took me out of the scribes' profession") when you were never in it, that is: he did not make me one of its people nor [put me] in it.

akhfash:258-258.t: He said: ﴿فَبَهَتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَ﴾, that is: Ibrāhīm dumbfounded him; and ﴿بُهِتَ﴾ is better and more frequent.

akhfash:259-259.t:
He said: ﴿أَوْ كَٱلَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ﴾. The kāf is redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رِبِّهِ﴾ ﴿أَوْ كَٱلَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ﴾, and the kāf is redundant. In the Book of Allah is ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ﴾; He is saying "there is nothing like Him", because Allah has no like.
And He said: ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾. The hāʾ is kept for the pause (hāʾ al-sakt), and when you continue you drop it, like ﴿إخْشَهْ﴾. Some kept it in continuous speech and said ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ وَٱنْظُرْ﴾, making the hāʾ part of the root; that in meaning is: the years have not passed over it. As for "السَّنَةُ" (year), some make it from wāw and say "سُنَيَّةٌ" (diminutive), and some make it from hāʾ and say "سُنَيْهَةٌ", making what dropped from it a hāʾ, as though he replaced the wāw with it, just as they said "أَسْنَتُوا" when years [of drought] befell them, replacing the hāʾ with tāʾ. They say "بِعْتُه مُساناةً" and "مُسانَهَةً" ("I sold it to him on yearly terms"). And ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾ can be [read] with this hāʾ being for the pause. The reading of those who continued with the hāʾ is taken as a concealed pause; and we read with the hāʾ in continuous speech.
And He said: ﴿وَٱنْظُرْ إِلَىٰ حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَٱنْظُرْ إِلَى ٱلعِظَامِ كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُهَا﴾, from "نَشَرْتُ", which is the opposite of "طَوَيْتُ" ("I folded"). Some read ﴿نُنْشِزُها﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the explanation fits a reading with rāʾ, such as نَنْشُرُها or نُنْشِرُها], because "فَعَلْتُ" and "أَفْعَلْتُ" often come together with one meaning; you say "صَدَدْتُ" and "أَصْدَدْتُ"; and He has said ﴿ثُمَّ إِذَا شَآءَ أَنشَرَهُ﴾. Some read ﴿نُنْشِرُها﴾ [Translator's note: the explanation "we raise them" and the examples نَشَزَ / أَنْشَزْتُ fit the reading with zāy], that is: we raise them. You say "نَشَزَ هذا" ("this rose up") and "أَنْشَزْتُهُ" ("I raised it").
And He said: ﴿أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾, when he means himself. Some read ﴿قال اعْلَمْ﴾ in the jussive, as an imperative, just as one says "Know that such-and-such has happened", as though saying it to someone else while only alerting himself. The jussive is better in meaning, except that it is less common in the reading; the nominative is the reading of the generality, and it is how we read.

akhfash:260-260.t:
As for His saying ﴿رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِـي ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾, that was not doubt on his part, and he did not mean by it seeing with the heart; he only meant seeing with the eye.
And Allah the Mighty and Majestic's saying to him ﴿أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن﴾: He is saying "Have you not believed?", that is: you are so. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; it is the thirty-third shāhid]:
أَلَسْتُمْ خيرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ المطَايا * وَأَنْدى العالمِينَ بُطُونَ راحِ
(Are you not the best of those who ride mounts, and the most generous-palmed of all the world?)
And His saying ﴿لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾, that is: my heart urges me to see, and when I have seen my heart will be at rest.
He said: ﴿فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ﴾, that is: cut them up; you say from it "صارَ", "يَصُورُ". Some read ﴿فَصُرْهُنَّ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the reading meant is presumably فَصِرْهُنَّ with kasra], making it from "صارَ", "يَصِيرُ". He said ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ because He means: "Take four to yourself and cut them up."

akhfash:264-264.t: He said: ﴿كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ﴾; the singular is "صَفْوانةٌ". Some make "الصَّفْوان" singular and take it as "the stone"; whoever makes it plural takes it as "stones", like "التَمْرَةِ" and "التَمْر" (date / dates). They have said "الكَذَّانِ" – "الكَذَّانَةُ", which is something like stone made of clay.

akhfash:265-265.t:
He said: ﴿كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ﴾. Some read ﴿بِرَبْوة﴾, ﴿بِرِبْوة﴾, ﴿بِرِباوة﴾ and ﴿بِرَباوة﴾; each is from the dialects of the Arabs, and all of it is from "الرابية" (a hill), its verb being "رَبا", "يَرْبو".
He said: ﴿فَآتَتْ أُكُلَهَا ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾, and He said ﴿مُخْتَلِفاً أُكُلُهُ﴾. "الأُكْلُ" is what is eaten, and "الأَكْلُ" is the action that comes from you. You say "أَكَلْتُ أَكْلاً" ("I ate an eating") and "أَكَلْت أَكْلَةً واحدةً" ("I ate one time"); and when you mean the food you say "أُكْلَةً واحدةً" ("one mouthful"). [The poet] said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the one hundred and forty-eighth shāhid]:
 ما أَكْلَةٌ أَكَلْتُها بِغنيمَةٍ * ولا جَوْعَةٌ أنْ جَعْتُها بِغَرامِ
(No meal I ate is a booty, and no hunger, if I went hungry, is a ruinous loss.)
He gave the alif fatḥa because he means the action; "وَلا جَوْعَةٌ" points you to that. If you wish you may give "الأكْلَةَ" ḍamma and mean by it the food.
And [He said: ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ يُصِبْهَا وَابِلٌ فَطَلٌّ ﴾].
You say concerning "الوابِل", which is heavy rain: "وَبَلَتْ السماء" and "أَوْبَلَتْ" ("the sky rained heavily"), like "مَطَرَتْ" and "أَمْطَرَتْ"; "طَلَّتْ" and "أَطَلَّتْ" from "الطَلّ" (drizzle); "غاثَتْ" and "أَغاثَتْ" from "الغَيْث" (rain). And you say "وُبِلَتْ الأرض" ("the land was rained on heavily"), so it is "مَوْبُولَةٌ", like "وُثِئَتْ رِجْلُهُ" ("his foot was sprained"); [and] "وَبَلَتْ" [in this sense] does not occur. His saying ﴿أَخْذاً وَبِيلا﴾ is from this, meaning: severe.

akhfash:266-266.t: He said: ﴿لَهُ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَاتِ وَأَصَابَهُ ٱلْكِبَرُ وَلَهُ ذُرِّيَّةٌ ضُعَفَآءُ فَأَصَابَهَآ إِعْصَارٌ فِيهِ نَارٌ فَٱحْتَرَقَتْ﴾, and He said in another place ﴿ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعافاً﴾. Both are the same, because you say "ظَريفٌ" – "ظِرافٌ" and "ظُرَفاءُ" (witty); that is how "فَعِيل" is pluralised.

akhfash:268-268.t: He said: ﴿ٱلشَّيْطَانُ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱلْفَقْرَ﴾. Some read ﴿الفُقْر﴾, like "الضَعْف" and "الضُعْف". He made "يَعِدُ" pass on to two objects.

akhfash:270-270.t:
He said: ﴿وَمَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ مِّن نَّفَقَةٍ أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِّن نَّذْرٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُهُ﴾. You make the statement [i.e. the pronoun] refer to the last, just as He said ﴿وَمَن يَكْسِبْ خَطِيۤئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئاً﴾. If you wish, you may make its masculine refer to "earning" in meaning, just as He said ﴿إِن تُبْدُواْ ٱلصَّدَقَاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ وَإِن تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا ٱلْفُقَرَآءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾; He is saying: "then giving is better for you, and concealing".
And His saying ﴿وَمَآ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْحِكْمَةِ يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ﴾: this [pronoun] refers to ﴿ما﴾. And His saying ﴿أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ﴾: you say "نَذَرَ", "يَنْذُرُ على نفْسِهِ", "نَذْراً" ("he vowed upon himself"), and "نَذَرْتُ مالي" ("I vowed my wealth"), so "أَنَا أَنْذَرُهُ" "نَذْراً"; Yūnus told us that from the Arabs. In the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is ﴿إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّراً﴾. The poet said [in the majzūʾ al-kāmil metre; it is the one hundred and forty-ninth shāhid]:
هُمْ يَنْذُرُونَ دَمي وَأَنْذُرُ أَنْ * لَقِيتُ بأَنْ أَشُدَّا
(They vow my blood, and I vow, if I meet [them], to attack.)
And ʿAntara said [in the kāmil metre; it is the one hundred and fiftieth shāhid]:
الشاتِمِيْ عِرْضِي وَلَمْ أَشْتِمُهما * وَالنَّاذِرَيْنِ إذا لَمْ الْقَهُما دَمِي
(The two who revile my honour though I have not reviled them, and who vow my blood when I am not meeting them.)

akhfash:274-274.t: And He said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بِٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ سِرّاً وَعَلاَنِيَةً فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾. He put the khabar (predicate) with the fāʾ since the noun is "الذي" and its ṣila (relative clause) is a verb, because it has the meaning of "مَنْ" (whoever); and "مَنْ" takes its answer with the fāʾ in conditional sentences (al-mujāzāt), because its meaning is "whoever spends his wealth, for him is such-and-such". And He said ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ مَاتُواْ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ فَلَن يَغْفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾, and He said ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَلَن يُضِلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾. This is plentiful in the Qur'an and in speech; like it is "الذي يأتينا فله درهم" ("whoever comes to us, he gets a dirham").

akhfash:279-279.t:
He said: ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ فَأْذَنُواْ بِحَرْبٍ﴾. You say "قَدْ أَذِنْتُ مِنْكَ بِحَرْبٍ" ("I have been notified of war from you") and "هو يَأْذَنُ".
And He said: ﴿لاَ تَظْلِمُونَ وَلاَ تُظْلَمُونَ﴾. Some read ﴿لا تُظْلَمُونَ ولا تَظْلِمون﴾; all of it is the same in meaning.

akhfash:280-280.t:
He said: ﴿وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَىٰ مَيْسَرَةٍ﴾. He is saying: "And if among those you claim from there is someone in hardship, then it is upon you to grant respite until ease." Some read ﴿فَنَظْرَة﴾. If you wish, you need not give "كان" an implied khabar, and you make "كانَ" equivalent to "وَقَعَ" ("occurred"). Some read ﴿مَيْسُرِهِ﴾, and that is not permissible, because there is no "مَفْعُلٌ" in the language. Had they read it ﴿مُوسَرِهِ﴾ it would be permissible, because it is from "أيْسَرَ", like "أدْخَلَ", whence "هُو مُدْخَل". Some read ﴿فَناظِرْهُ الى مَيْسَرَةٍ﴾ and ﴿مَيْسَرَةٍ﴾, making it "فاعِلْ" from "نَاظَرَ" and putting it in the jussive as an imperative.
And He said: ﴿وَأَن تَصَدَّقُواْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾. He is saying: "charity is better for you". He made ﴿أَنْ تَصَدَّقُواْ﴾ a noun that is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and made ﴿خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

akhfash:282-282.t:
He said: ﴿وَٱسْتَشْهِدُواْ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ﴾, that is: if the two witnesses are not two men. ﴿َفَرَجُلٌ وَٱمْرَأَتَانِ﴾: then the one called to witness is a man and two women.
And He said: ﴿وَلاَ تَسْأَمُوۤاْ﴾, because it is from "سَئِمْتُ", "تَسْأَمُ", "سَآمةً", "سَأْمَةً", "سَآماً" and "سَأْماً" (to grow weary).
[And He said]: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ﴾: jussive because it is a prohibition. When you pause you say "يَأْبَ", pausing without yāʾ.
And He said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَارَةٌ حَاضِرَةٌ﴾, that is: [unless] present trade takes place. The accusative may also occur in it, on [the basis of] an implied noun: "unless that is present trade" ("إلاّ أنْ تَكُونَ تلكَ تِجارةً").
And He said: ﴿وَلاَ يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلاَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ as a prohibition; the nominative [would be] as a statement. It is like ﴿لاَ تُضَآرَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا﴾, except that ﴿لا تُضارُّ﴾ has not been read in the nominative. [Translator's note: so in the text; the nominative لا تُضارُّ in 2:233 is in fact a known reading, and al-Akhfash himself discusses it as nominative under 2:233.]
And His saying ﴿إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ﴾: His saying ﴿بِدَيْنٍ﴾ is tawkīd (emphasis), like His saying ﴿فَسَجَدَ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ﴾, because you say "تَدايَنَّا" ("we contracted debts with each other"), and that indicates your saying "with a debt". The poet said [in the rajaz metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-first shāhid]:
دَايَنْتُ أَرْوَى والدُّيونُ تُقْضَى * [فَمَطَلَتْ بَعْضاً وَأَدَّتْ بَعْضَا]
(I gave Arwā credit — and debts are to be paid — [and she delayed some and paid some].)
You say it: "I lent to her and she lent to me, so we have contracted debts with each other", just as you say "I met her and she met me, so we have met each other".
And He said: ﴿أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيراً أَو كَبِيراً إِلَىٰ أَجَلِهِ﴾, and He left "the witness" implied. He said ﴿إِلَىٰ أَجَلِهِ﴾: to the term at which his testimony is valid; and Allah knows best.

akhfash:283-283.t:
He said: ﴿فَرِهَانٌ مَّقْبُوضَةٌ﴾. You say "رَهْنٌ" – "رِهانٌ" (pledge, pledges), like "حَبْلٌ" – "حِبالٌ" (rope, ropes). Abū ʿAmr read "فَرُهُنٌ", and that is ugly, because "فَعْلٌ" is not pluralised on "فُعُل" except rarely and anomalously. He claimed that they say "سَقْفٌ" – "سُقُفٌ" (roof, roofs), and they read this verse ﴿سَقْفاً مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾; and they said "قَلْبٌ" – "قُلُبٌ", "قَلْبٌ" being from "the heart (pith) of the palm tree", and "لَحْد" – "لُحُد" for "the niche of the grave"; this is anomalous and hardly known. They have pluralised "فَعْلٌ" on "فُعْلٌ", saying "ثَطٌّ" – "ثُطٌّ" (thin-bearded), "جَوْنٌ" – "جُونٌ" (black) and "وَرْدٌ" – "وُرْدٌ" (bay-coloured). "رُهُنٌ" may be a plural of "الرِّهانِ", as though it were a plural of the plural; and "رِهانٌ" is better than this forced usage. They have said "سَهْمٌ خَشْنٌ" in [the plural] "سِهامٍ خُشْنٍ" ("rough arrows"), lightened. Abū ʿAmr said: "The Arabs said 'رُهُنٌ' to distinguish it from the stakes (rihān) of horse-racing." Al-Akhfash said: "Every plural on 'فُعْل' can also be said as 'فُعُل'."
And He said: ﴿فلْيُؤَدِّ ٱلَّذِي ٱؤْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ﴾. It is from "أَدّى", "يُؤدِّي", which is why it has hamza. And "اؤْتُمِنَ" — he gave it hamza because it is from "الأَمانَةِ" (trust), [and] the place of its first radical (fāʾ) is a hamza; except that when you begin with it, the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) stands in it, so you do not pronounce the hamza in the place of the fāʾ, lest two hamzas come together.

akhfash:285-285.t: He said: ﴿غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا﴾. He made it a substitute for pronouncing the verb, as though He had said: "Forgive us, Your forgiveness, our Lord." [And] like it is "سُبْحانَكَ", which is really "تسبيحَك", that is: "we glorify You Your glorification"; and it is declaring [You] free and exalted [from all imperfection].

akhfash:30-30.t:
As for the angels' saying ﴿أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا﴾, that was not an objection on their part against their Lord; they only asked in order to know, and they reported about themselves that they glorify and sanctify. Or they said that because they disliked that Allah should be disobeyed, since the jinn had been commanded before that and had disobeyed.
As for His words ﴿نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ﴾, and He said ﴿وَٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾, and He said ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ﴾: that is because all remembrance (dhikr) is glorification (tasbīḥ) and prayer. You say "قَضَيْتُ سُبْحتي من الذكِر والصَلاة" (I completed my devotions of remembrance and prayer). So He said "سَبِّح بالحَمْد" (glorify with praise), i.e. "let your devotion be with praise of Allah". His words ﴿أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا﴾ came by way of affirmation, as the poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the thirty-third evidentiary verse]:
أَلَسْتُمْ خيرَ مَن رَكِبَ المطايا * وأنْدى العالَمِينَ بطونَ راحِ
(Are you not the best of those who ride mounts, and the most open-handed of all the world?)
i.e. you are so.

akhfash:31-31.t:
His words ﴿ٱلأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ﴾: He means that He presented to them the bearers of the names; what shows you that is His words ﴿أَنْبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَآءِ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾. That was not because the angels had claimed anything; He was only making known their ignorance of the knowledge of the unseen, and His knowledge of that and His act. So He said ﴿أَنْبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَآءِ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ إِن كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾, as a man says to another man "أَنْبِئْني بهذا إنْ كنتَ تَعْلَم" (tell me this, if you know), knowing that he does not know, meaning that he is ignorant. At that they extolled Him and said ﴿سُبْحَانَكَ لاَ عِلْمَ لَنَآ﴾ of the unseen accordingly, "and we know that we have no knowledge of the unseen", reporting about themselves in the manner in which Allah reported about them. His words ﴿سُبْحَانَكَ لاَ عِلْمَ لَنَآ﴾: He made "سبحانَكَ" accusative because He meant "نسبِّحكَ" (we glorify You); He made it a substitute for pronouncing the verb, as though He said "نُسَبِّحُكَ بسُبْحانِكَ", but "سُبْحان" is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is not declined. "سُبْحان" in exegesis means declaring free and exalting above [any imperfection]. The poet said [in the sarīʿ metre; this is the thirty-fourth evidentiary verse]:
أقولُ لَمّا جاءني فَخْرُه * سُبحانَ من عَلْقَمةَ الفاخِرِ
(I say, when his boasting reached me: how far removed [I am] from ʿAlqama the boaster!)
He means: disavowal of him.

akhfash:34-34.t:
This is the chapter on exception (istithnāʾ).
His words ﴿فَسَجَدُواْ إِلاَّ إِبْلِيسَ﴾: it is accusative because you occupied the verb with them and away from him, so you took him out of the verb from among them, as you say "جاءَ القومُ إلاّ زيداً" (the people came, except Zayd). For when you assigned the verb to them and occupied it with them, and something other than them came after them, you likened it to the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) after the fāʿil (agent), when you have occupied the verb with it.
His words ﴿أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ﴾: ﴿استكبرَ﴾ was given fatḥa because every "فَعَلَ" or "فُعِلَ" [past verb] has fatḥa [at its end], as in ﴿قَالَ رَجُلاَنِ﴾, ﴿ٱلَّذِي ٱؤْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ﴾, ﴿ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ﴾ and ﴿وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾, because all of this is "فَعَلَ" and "فُعِلَ".

akhfash:35-35.t:
The chapter on the vocative (al-duʿāʾ)
His words ﴿يَا آدَمُ ٱسْكُنْ﴾, ﴿يَآءَادَمُ أَنبِئْهُمْ﴾ and ﴿يٰفِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّي رَسُولٌ﴾: all of these took the nominative form (ḍamma) only because it is a single [non-construct] noun, and the single noun takes ḍamma in the vocative while being in an accusative position; but it was treated like the nouns that are not fully declinable. When it is muḍāf (in a genitive construct), it is accusative, because that is the original. He only means "أعني فلانا" (I mean so-and-so) and "أدعو" (I call). That is like His words ﴿يَٰأَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لاَ تَأْمَنَّا﴾ and ﴿رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَآ أَنفُسَنَا﴾, by which He only means "يا ربِّنا ظَلَمْنا أَنْفُسَنا" (O our Lord, we have wronged ourselves), and His words "رَبَّنا تَقبِّلْ مِنّا".
This is the chapter on the fāʾ
His words ﴿وَلاَ تَقْرَبَا هَـٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْظَّالِمِينَ﴾: this is what the grammarians call "the answer with fāʾ" (jawāb al-fāʾ). It is what comes as an answer to the command, the prohibition, the question, the wish, negation and denial. All of that is accusative by an implied "أنْ"; likewise the wāw, even though its meaning is not like the meaning of the fāʾ. This is accusative only because the fāʾ and the wāw are conjunctions, so the speaker intended what preceded in his speech to be a noun, as though he said "لا يكُنْ منكما قربُ الشجرة" (let there be no approaching of the tree from you two); then he wanted to conjoin the verb to the noun, so he implied "أَنْ" with the verb, because "أَنْ" with the verb is a noun [i.e. an interpreted maṣdar], so he conjoins a noun to a noun. This is the explanation of everything made accusative after the wāw and the fāʾ. Similar to that are His words ﴿لاَ تَفْتَرُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍ﴾, which is the answer to a prohibition, and ﴿لاَ يُقْضَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُواْ﴾, the answer to a negation. The explanation is what I have mentioned to you.
When it is fitting to make the second follow the first, it is permissible to make it like it, as in His words ﴿وَدُّواْ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾, i.e. "وَدُّوا لَوْ يُدْهِنُونَ" (they wished that they might compromise), and as in His words ﴿وَدَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ عَنْ أَسْلِحَتِكُمْ وَأَمْتِعَتِكُمْ فَيَمِيلُونَ﴾: He made the first a verb and did not intend it as a noun, so He conjoined the verb to the verb, which is the wish, as though He said "وَدُّوا لو تَغْفَلونَ وَلَوْ يَمِيلُونَ" (they wished that you would be heedless and that they might fall upon you). And He said ﴿لاَ يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ﴾, i.e. "لا يؤذَن لَهُمْ ولا يَعْتَذِرُونَ" (they will not be permitted, nor will they excuse themselves). As for what comes after the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a conditional with fāʾ and wāw, you may also, if you wish, make it accusative by an implied "أن", when you intend to make the first a noun, as He said ﴿إِن يَشَأْ يُسْكِنِ ٱلرِّيحَ فَيَظْلَلْنَ رَوَاكِدَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهِ﴾ ﴿أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ [بِمَا كَسَبُوا]* وَيَعْفُ عَن كَثِيرٍ﴾ ﴿وَيَعْلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: the asterisk appears thus in the source], making it accusative; had He made it jussive by conjunction it would have been permissible, and had He made it nominative as resumptive (mubtadaʾ) it would also have been permissible. And He said ﴿وَإِن تُبْدُواْ مَا فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ﴾: you make ﴿فَيَغفِر﴾ jussive (majzūm) when you intend conjunction, accusative when you imply "إنْ" [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for "أنْ"] and intend the first to be a noun, and nominative as resumptive; all of that is the speech of the Arabs. And He said ﴿قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَيُخْزِهِمْ وَيَنْصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, then He said ﴿وَيَتُوبُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾: He made ﴿وَيَتُوبُ﴾ nominative because it is a new, resumptive statement, not in the sense of the first; He does not mean "قاتلوهم يتبْ الله عليهم" (fight them and Allah will turn to them). Had it been this, the jussive would have been permissible in it for the reason I mentioned. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the thirty-fifth evidentiary verse]:
فإِنْ يهلِكْ أبو قابوس يهلِكْ * ربيعُ الناسِ والشَهْرُ الحرامُ
ونُمْسِكَ بعدَه بذِنابِ عيشٍ * أجبِّ الظهرِ ليس له سنامُ
(If Abū Qābūs perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred month perish; and after him we hold on to the tail-end of a life like a camel with a cut-down back, having no hump.)
He made "ونمسكَ" accusative by an implied "أَنْ", and we see that he makes the first a noun; the jussive by conjunction and the nominative as resumptive are also possible in it. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the thirty-sixth evidentiary verse]:
ومَنْ يَغتربْ عن قومِهِ لا يَزَلْ يرى * مصارعَ مظلومٍ مجرّا ومَسْحُبا
ومَنْ يغتربْ عن قومِهِ لا يَجِدْ لهُ * على مَنْ لهُ رَهْطٌ حواليهِ مغْضبا
وتُدْفنُ منه المحسَنات وان يُسِىءْ * يَكُنْ ما أساءَ النار في رأسِ كَبْكَبا
(Whoever goes abroad from his people will not cease to see the downfall of a wronged man, dragged and pulled along; whoever goes abroad from his people will find none to be angry on his behalf against one who has a clan around him; his good deeds are buried, and if he does wrong, his wrong is like a fire on the summit of Kabkab.)
"تُدفنُ" admits all the forms. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the thirty-seventh evidentiary verse]:
فإن يَرْجعِ النعمان نَفْرَحْ ونَبْتَهِجْ * ويأتِ مَعَدّاً مُلْكُها وربيعُها
وإِنْ يَهْلِكِ النعمانُ تُعْرَ مَطِيَّةٌ * وتُخْبَأُ في جوفِ العياب قُطُوعها
(If al-Nuʿmān returns, we shall rejoice and be glad, and Maʿadd will receive its kingship and its spring; and if al-Nuʿmān perishes, the mounts will be left unsaddled and their saddle-cloths hidden away in the bags.)
Allah the Blessed and Exalted said ﴿وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْهُ﴾: this can only be nominative, because it is the apodosis which cannot be dispensed with. When the fāʾ is the apodosis of a conditional, what follows it is always a mubtadaʾ (subject); that is the fāʾ of inception, not the fāʾ of conjunction. Do you not see that you say "ان تأتِني فأمُركَ عندي على ما تحبُّ" (if you come to me, your affair with me will be as you like)? If this were the fāʾ of conjunction, it would not be permissible to stop until you brought an apodosis for what follows "إنْ". Similar to it is ﴿وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلاً﴾. Some read ﴿فَأُمَتِّعُهُ ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُ﴾: [with] ﴿أَضْطَرُّهُ﴾, when he makes the alif connecting, he makes it an imperative. In this reading, when he means the imperative, both ḍamma and fatḥa are permissible in it. However, the alif is a connecting alif, and "ثُمَّ" only made it disjunctive in the other reading, because everything whose meaning is "أَفْعَلُ" (I do) is disjunctive, whether it is from a connecting or a disjunctive [verb]. He said ﴿أَنَاْ آتِيكَ بِهِ﴾, which is from "أتى" "يأتي"; and He said ﴿أَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِ آلِهَةً﴾, leaving the alif after the interrogative alif because it is the alif of "أفعل". And Allah the Blessed* and Exalted said, relating about the disbelievers [Translator's note: the asterisk appears thus in the source]: ﴿لَوْلاۤ أَخَّرْتَنِيۤ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّالِحِينَ﴾. His words ﴿فَأَصَّدَّقَ﴾ are the answer to the question, because ﴿لَوْلاۤ﴾ here is like "هلا" (why not), and ﴿وَأَكُن﴾ is conjoined to the position of ﴿فَأَصَّدَّقَ﴾, because the answer to a question, when it has no fāʾ, is jussive. Some read ﴿فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُونَ﴾, conjoining it to what follows the fāʾ, and that goes against the written text (muṣḥaf). And ﴿مَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَلاَ هَادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرُهُمْ﴾ has been read in the jussive: ﴿يَذَرْهُم﴾ is jussive as conjoined to the position of the fāʾ, because its position is jussive when it is the apodosis of a conditional. Whoever makes it nominative, conjoining it to what follows the fāʾ — that is better, and it is a [recognised] reading. And He said ﴿وَإِن تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا ٱلْفُقَرَآءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنكُم﴾, jussive and nominative, as I have explained. In this and in the word before it the accusative is also permissible, because it has come after the apodosis of a conditional, like ﴿وَيَعْلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا﴾ [and] ﴿وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَاهَدُواْ مِنكُمْ وَيَعْلَمَ ٱلصَّابِرِينَ﴾: the second is accusative because He intended the first to be like a noun, and in the second there is the wāw. If you wish you may make it jussive by conjunction, as though you said "ولمّا يعلمِ الصابرين". If someone says: "'ولما يَعْلمِ الله الصابرين', ﴿وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَاهَدُواْ مِنكُمْ﴾ — so does He not know them?", I say: Indeed He knew; but this, according to what the people of interpretation mention, is in order to make it clear to people, as though He said "ليَعْلَمَه الناسُ" (so that people may know it), just as He said ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَىٰ لِمَا لَبِثُواْ أَمَداً﴾, while He already knew, but in order to make that clear. Some people read things like this in the Quran as ﴿لِيُعْلَم أَيُّ الحزبين﴾ (so that it may be known which of the two parties), and I think they only read it so out of ignorance of the other approach.
Among what has come with the wāw*: ﴿وَلاَ تَلْبِسُواْ ٱلْحَقَّ بِٱلْبَاطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُواْ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾. [Translator's note: the asterisk appears thus in the source.] If you wish you may make ﴿وَتَكْتُمُواْ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾ accusative, when you intend the first to be a noun, implying "أَنْ" with ﴿تَكْتُمُوا﴾ so that it becomes a noun. And if you wish you may conjoin it, making it jussive [by conjunction] with the verb before it. He said ﴿أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ﴾, conjoining the saying to the jussive verb and so making it jussive. They claimed that in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is ﴿وَأَقُولُ لَّكُمآ﴾, by an implied "أَن", intending the first to be a noun. [Translator's note: so in the source; "وأقولُ" as printed would be nominative, whereas the explanation by implied أن requires "وأقولَ".] The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the thirty-eighth evidentiary verse]:
لقد كان في حَوْلٍ ثَواءٍ ثويته * تَقَضِّي لُباناتٍ وَيَسْأمَ سائِمُ
(In a whole year of staying that I stayed there was the fulfilment of needs, and [enough] for one who tires to grow tired.)
— ثواءٌ, ثواءً or ثواءٍ: nominative, accusative and genitive — he made it [يسأمَ] accusative by an implied "أَنْ", because "التقضي" (fulfilment) is a noun. Whoever said "فَتُقْضى" (so needs are fulfilled) made "ويسأمُ" nominative, because he conjoined it to a verb; and this is an affirmative statement. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the thirty-ninth evidentiary verse]:
فإِنْ لم أصدِّقْ ظَنَّكُمْ بتَيقُّنٍ * فَلا سَقَتِ الأوْصالَ مِنّي الرّواعِدُ
ويَعلمَ أكفائي من الناسِ أَنَّني * أَنَا الفارسُ الحامي الذمارِ المذاودُ
(If I do not confirm your opinion with certainty, may the thunder-clouds not water my limbs — and [may it be that] my peers among men know that I am the horseman who guards what is sacred, the defender.)
And the poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the fortieth evidentiary verse]:
فإن يقدِرْ عليكَ أبو قُبَيْسٍ * نَمُطَّ بِكَ المَنِيَّة في هَوانِ
وَتُخْضَبَ لِحيَةٌ غَدَرَتْ وخانتْ * بِأَحْمَرَ من نَجِيعِ الجَوْفِ آنِ
(If Abū Qubays gets the better of you, death will drag you away in disgrace, and a beard that was treacherous and false will be dyed with red, hot blood from the body's depths.)
He made all of this accusative because he intended the first to be a noun, so he implied "أنْ" after the wāw so that it would be a noun like the first, and conjoined it to it. As for His words ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ ﴾ and ﴿فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, this is as the answer to a wish, because its meaning is "لَيْتَ لَنّا كَرَّةً" (would that we had a return). The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the forty-first evidentiary verse]:
فلستُ بمدركٍ ما فاتَ مني * بـ"لهفَ" ولا بـ"ليتَ" ولا "لواني"
(I shall not recover what has escaped me by "alas", nor by "would that", nor by "if only I…")
He treated "لوَاني" like "ليْتَ", because when a man says "لَو أنّي كنتُ فعلتُ كذا وكذا" (if only I had done such-and-such), you only mean "ودِدتُ لو كنتُ فَعلْتُ" (I wish I had done). The implied "أَنْ" is permissible only in non-affirmative [speech], because in non-affirmative speech what follows comes contrary to what precedes, contradicting it.
So when a contrast to its beginning arises in it, this implication is permissible. In affirmative [speech], its end follows its beginning, as in the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَتُصْبِحُ ٱلأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً﴾: the meaning is "إسمعوا أنزلَ اللّهُ من السماءِ ماءً" (hear: Allah sent down water from the sky); this is an affirmative statement, and ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ is a call to attention. The affirmative may be made accusative in poetry. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the forty-second evidentiary verse]:
سأترُكُ منزلي لِبني تَميمٍ * وأَلْحَقُ بالحجاز فأستريحا
(I shall leave my home to the Banū Tamīm and join the Hijaz, and so be at rest.)
This is hardly known, but it is permissible in poetry. Ṭarafa said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the forty-third evidentiary verse]:
لها هَضْبَةٌ لا يَدْخُلُ الذُلُّ وَسْطَها * ويأوى اليها المستجيرُ فيُعْصَما
(It has a highland into whose midst humiliation does not enter, and the refugee shelters in it and is protected.)
Know that making the implied "أن" explicit is not permissible in any place where it is implied after the fāʾ. Do you not see that when you say "لا تأتِه فيضرِبَك" (do not go to him, lest he strike you), it is not permissible to say "لا تأْتِه فأنْ يضرِبَكَ"? You only made it accusative by "أنْ", but it is not good [Translator's note: the source has "يسحن", a misprint for "يحسن"] to make it explicit — just as it is not permissible, in your saying "عسى أنْ تفعلَ" (perhaps you will do), [to say] "عسى الفعل", nor, in your saying "ما كان ليفعل" (he was not one to do), [to say] "ما كان لان يفعل", nor to make explicit the noun that is in your saying "نعم رجلاً" (what an excellent man). Many an implied element is not made explicit, because the speech was framed on its being implied; if it were made explicit, that would be contrary to how it was framed in wording, and ambiguity would enter it.

akhfash:79-79.t:
﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾: "الويلُ" (woe) is nominative because it is a noun that is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and He made what follows it its khabar (predicate). Likewise "الوَيْحُ", "الوَيْلُ" and "الوَيْسُ": when this lām comes after them, you put them in the nominative. As for "التَعْسُ" (perdition), "البُعْدُ" (remoteness) and what resembles them, they are always accusative. That is because everything of this kind whose annexation without a lām is good is nominative with the lām and accusative without the lām, as in ﴿وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾ and "وَيْلٌ لِزَيْدٍ" ("woe to Zayd"); if you dropped the lām you would say "ويلَ زيدٍ", "ويحَ زيدٍ" and "ويسَ زيدٍ". Its annexation without a lām is good, and so you put it in the nominative with the lām, as in ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾. As for His saying ﴿أَلاَ بُعْداً لِّمَدْيَنَ﴾, ﴿أَلاَ بُعْداً لِّثَمُودَ﴾ and ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَتَعْساً لَّهُمْ﴾, the annexation of this without a lām is not good: if you said "تَعْسَهُم" or "بُعْدَهُم", it would not be good. All of this is accusative by the verb, as though you said "may Allah make them perish a perishing" and "may Allah put them far away a putting far". And when you say "ويْلَ زيدٍ", it is as though you said "may Allah fasten woe upon him". As for your putting it in the nominative with the lām, that is only because you made it something occurring and binding upon them by desert. It is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and what follows it is built upon it. Some people put it in the accusative with an implied verb, and that is good analogy; they say "وَيْلاً لزيد" and "وَيْحاً لِزيد". The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the ninety-ninth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
كَسَا اللُؤْمُ تَيْماً خُضْرَةً في جُلُودها * فَوَيْلاً لِتَيْمٍ من سرابيلها الخُضْرِ
(Baseness has clothed Taym with a darkness in their skins — so woe to Taym from their dark garments!)
Al-Akhfash said: "ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar told me that he heard the Bedouins recite it thus, in the accusative." And some of them put in the nominative what is accusative in this chapter. Abū Zubayd said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundredth shāhid]:
أَغارَ وأَقْوى ذات يومٍ وخَيْبَةٌ * لأوَّلِ مَنْ يَلْقى غيٌ مُيَسَّرُ
(He raided, and one day he was left destitute — and disappointment to the first he meets; error is made easy [for him].)
Chapter on the lām.
And His saying ﴿لِيَشْتَرُواْ بِهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً﴾: when this lām has the meaning of "كَيْ" ("so that"), what comes after it is accusative by an implied "أَنْ"; likewise what is accusative by "كيْ" is also by an implied "أَنْ". It is as though He said "for the purchase", for "يَشتَرُوا" can only be a noun by means of "أنْ"; so "أَنْ" is implied, it is what makes [the verb] accusative, and it is in the position of the genitive by the lām. Likewise ﴿كَيْ لاَ يَكُونَ دُولَةً﴾: "أَنْ" is implied, and "كيْ" has put it in the genitive. And they said "كَيْمَهْ" ("for what?"), "مَهْ" being a noun because it is the interrogative "ما", and "كَيْ" was annexed to it. And "كَيْ" may be in the position of "أَنْ", itself being what makes the verb accusative, and that is His saying ﴿لِّكَيْلاَ تَأْسَوْاْ﴾, where He made the lām fall on it; if "كَيْ" and what follows it were not a noun, the lām would not fall on it. Likewise what is accusative after "حتّى" is only accusative by an implied "أَنْ". He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ ٱللَّهِ﴾ and ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَتَّبِعَ مِلَّتَهُمْ﴾: it is only "until that [it] comes" and "until that you follow", and likewise everything in the Quran with "حتّى". Likewise ﴿وَزُلْزِلُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ﴾, i.e. "until that [he] says", because "حتّى" has the meaning of "إلى" ("to, until"): you say "أَقَمْنا حتّى الليلِ" ("we stayed until night"), i.e. "to the night". If it is said, "Making 'أَنْ' overt here is ugly", I say: "Things are sometimes implied whose overt expression is ugly, when they can do without them. Do you not see that your saying 'إنْ زيداً ضربْتَهُ' ('if Zayd — you struck him') is accusative by an implied verb which, if you made it overt, would not be good?" This verse has also been read ﴿وَزُلْزِلُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ﴾ [Translator's note: the text prints «يَقُولَ» here; the explanation that follows requires the nominative reading «يَقُولُ»], meaning "until the Messenger is saying", making what follows "حتّى" an inceptive clause. That may be like your saying "سِرْتُ حتّى أدْخُلُها" ("I travelled until I am entering it") when you mean "I travelled, and there I was entering it", and "سِرْتُ أمسِ حتّى أَدْخُلُها اليومَ" ("I travelled yesterday so that I enter it today"), i.e. so that "I today enter it and am not prevented". When it is the goal of the travelling, you put it in the accusative. Likewise what has not [yet] become actual of what "حتّى" falls on, as in ﴿لاۤ أَبْرَحُ حَتَّىٰ أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِىَ حُقُباً﴾. As for ﴿وَلَن يُخْلِفَ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ﴾, it is accusative by "لَنْ", just as it is accusative by "أنْ". Some of them said: it is only "أَنْ" to which "لا" was attached, as though He meant "لا أَنْ يُخْلِفَ اللّهُ وَعْدَهُ"; then, when it became frequent in speech, it was shortened. This is one view, and likewise every "لَنْ" in the Quran. But whoever holds that view ought to put in the nominative "أزيدٌ لَنْ تَضْرِبُ", because it has the meaning of "as for Zayd, there is no striking for him". Likewise what is accusative by "إذَنْ": you say "إذَنْ آتيَكَ" ("then I will come to you"), making [the verb] accusative by it as by "أَنْ" and "لَنْ". When the fāʾ or the wāw precedes it, you use the nominative, as in the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَإِذاً لاَّ تُمَتَّعُونَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾, and He said ﴿فَإِذاً لاَّ يُؤْتُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ نَقِيراً﴾; and in his view this may also be accusative by making "إذَنْ" govern. They have claimed that in some readings it is accusative; it is only nominative because the support of the verb came to be on the fāʾ and the wāw, and it was not made dependent on "إذَنْ", as though He said "so they would not give people, then, a speck" [and] "and you would not be given enjoyment, then". And His saying ﴿لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ أنْ لا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَيْءٍ﴾ [and] ﴿وَحَسِبُوۤاْ أنْ لا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ and ﴿أنْ لا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلاً﴾: the verb is nominative after "أنْ لا" because this ["أنْ"] is heavy in meaning, but it was lightened and the noun in it was made implied. The proof of that is that the noun and the heavy form are good in it: do you not see that you say "do they not see that it does not return to them", and you say "that they are not able to do anything" [and] "that there would be no trial"? And He said ﴿آيَتكَ أنْ لا تُكَلِّمَ الناسَ﴾: it is accusative because this is not in the meaning of the heavy one; it is only ﴿آيَتُكَ أنْ لا تُكَلِّمَ﴾ just as you say ﴿آيتُكَ أَنْ تُكَلِّمَ﴾, and ﴿لا﴾ was brought in for the intended meaning of negation. If you put this in the nominative, it would be permissible with the meaning "your sign is that you will not speak"; and if the other were put in the accusative, it would be permissible by making it the light "أنْ" that governs verbs. Like that is ﴿إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ﴾, and He said ﴿تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ﴾, and He said ﴿إِن ظَنَّآ أَن يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ﴾. And you say "عَلِمْت أَنْ لا تُكَرِّمُني" ("I knew that you would not honour me") and "حسِبْتُ أَنْ لا تُكْرِمُنِي" ("I reckoned that you would not honour me"); this is like what I mentioned to you. What follows "عَلِمْتُ" and "اسْتَيْقَنْتُ" ("I was certain") became nominative only because it is actual (wājib); and since it is actual, it would not be good for the "أنْ" that governs verbs to follow it, because that one only occurs in what is not actual. Do you not see that you say "I want you to come to me", and this is only for a matter that has not happened? And what follows thinking and the like is nominative because it resembles knowing, since one knows something of the thing when one thinks it. As for "خَشِيتُ أنْ لا تُكْرِمَني" ("I feared that you would not honour me"), this has not happened, so in the like of this the light "أن" governs; but if you put it in the nominative on [the basis of] a matter that is settled with you and that you know — as though you had tested him and he would not honour you — and you said "خَشِيتُ أنْ لا تُكْرِمُني", i.e. "I feared that you do not honour me", it would be permissible.
Yūnus claimed that some people among the Arabs give a fatḥa to the lām that stands in the place of "كَيْ", and they recited this verse, and he claimed that he heard it with the fatḥa [in the wāfir metre; it is the hundred and first shāhid]:
يُؤامِرُني رَبيعَةُ كُلَّ يَومٍ * لأُهْلِكَهُ وأَقْتِنيَ الدَّجاجا
(Rabīʿa consults me every day [urging me] to destroy it [my wealth] and acquire chickens.)
And Khalaf claimed that it is a dialect of the Banū al-ʿAnbar, and that he heard a man of them recite this verse with the fatḥa [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and second shāhid]:
فقُلْتُ لكَلْبِيَّيْ قُضاعَةَ إنَّما * تَخَبَّرْ تُماني أهْلَ فَلْجٍ لأَمْنَعا
(I said to the two Kalbīs of Quḍāʿa: you have only informed me about the people of Falj so that I would be held back.)
He means "about the people of Falj". I have myself heard that from the Arabs; and that is because the original vowel of the lām is the fatḥa, and it was only given a kasra in annexation [i.e. as a preposition] to distinguish it from the lām of ibtidāʾ. Abū ʿUbayda claimed that he heard the lām of "لعلَّ" with a fatḥa in the dialect of those who put what follows it in the genitive, in the saying of the poet [in the wāfir metre; it is the hundred and third shāhid]:
لِعَلَّ اللّهِ يُمْكِنُنِي عَلَيْها * جِهاراً من زُهَيْرٍ أَوْ أَسِيدِ
(Perhaps Allah will give me power over her openly, from Zuhayr or Asīd.)
[Translator's note: the verse is printed with «لِعَلَّ» (kasra), although the sentence introducing it speaks of hearing it with a fatḥa.]
He means "لِعَلَّ عبدِ اللّهِ" [Translator's note: printed thus]. This lām has the kasra because it is the lām of annexation; and he claimed that he heard it with a fatḥa, so it is like the lām of "كَيْ". We have heard among the Arabs one who uses the nominative after "كيما", and he recited [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and fourth shāhid]:
إذا أَنْتَ لم تَنْفَعْ فَضُرَّ فإنَّما * يُرَجّى الفَتَى كيما يَضُرُّ وَيَنْفَعُ
(If you do not benefit, then harm; for a young man is only hoped for so that he may harm and benefit.)
This one made "ما" a noun and made "يَضَرُّ" and "يَنْفَعُ" its ṣila (relative clause); he made it a noun for the verb, made "كَيْ" fall on it, and put "كَيْ" in the place of the lām. And His saying ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّهُ مَن يُحَادِدِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَأَنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ and His saying ﴿أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ سُوۤءًا بِجَهَالَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾: it is likely that the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), like the addition of "ما", and that what follows the fāʾ is a badal (substitute) for the "أن" before it. The best is to give "إن" the kasra and make the fāʾ the answer of the condition. They have claimed that they say "أَخُوكَ فوُجِد" and "بل أخوك فَجُهِدَ", meaning "your brother was found" and "rather your brother was exhausted", adding the fāʾ. And al-Ḥasan explained ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا﴾ as with the wāw dropped; he said: "Its meaning is: its keepers said to them", so the wāw in this is redundant. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and fifth shāhid]:
فإذا وَذَلِكَ يا كُبَيْشَةُ لَمْ يَكُنْ * إلاَّ كَلَمَّةِ حالِمٍ بِخَيالِ
(And then that, O Kubaysha, was nothing but like a dreamer's brief visit from a phantom.)
And he said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and sixth shāhid]:
فإذا وذلكَ ليسَ إلاّ حينُه * واذا مَضَى شَيْءٌ كأَنْ لَمْ يُفْعَلِ
(And then that is only for its time; and when a thing has passed, it is as if it had never been done.)
It is as though he added the wāw and made its khabar implied; and things like this whose khabar is implied are many.

akhfash:36-36.t:
As for His words ﴿ فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَانُ عَنْهَا﴾, He only means "الزَلَل" (slipping). You say "زَلَّ فلانُ" (so-and-so slipped) and "أَزْلَلْتُه" (I made him slip), and "زالَ فلانُ" (so-and-so moved away) and "أَزالَهُ فُلانُ" (so-and-so removed him). The doubled form is the good reading, and that is how we read. Some read
﴿فأزالَهُما﴾, taking it from "زَالَ، يزولُ" (to move away). You say "زالَ الرجلُ" (the man moved away) and "أزالَهُ فلان" (so-and-so removed him).
And He said ﴿ٱهْبِطُواْ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ ﴾: He only said ﴿ٱهْبِطُواْ﴾ [in the plural] — and Allah knows best — because Iblīs was the third of them; therefore He used the plural.

akhfash:37-37.t: His words ﴿فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ﴾: He made Adam the one who received. Some read ﴿آدمَ﴾ in the accusative and made "الكلمات" nominative, making them the ones that reached [him].

akhfash:38-38.t:
He said ﴿فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ﴾. That is because "إمّا" is in the position of a conditional; it is "إمّا", not "أَمَا"; it is "إنْ" with "ما" added to it, and the verb after it has come to take the light or heavy nūn [of emphasis], though it may be without the nūn. The nūn became good in it only when "ما" entered it, because "ما" is a negation, that is, something non-affirmative, and it is one of the particles that negate the affirmative; so the nūn became good in it, as in their saying "بِعينٍ مّا أَرَيَنَّك" (I shall surely see you soon): when "ما" was put in it, the nūn became good. Like "إمّا" here are His words ﴿فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلبَشَرِ أَحَداً﴾ and His words ﴿قُل رَّبِّ إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّي مَا يُوعَدُونَ رَبِّ فَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِي فِي ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾, where the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is in His words ﴿فَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِي﴾. There is much like this in the Quran and in speech. As for "إمّا" in a position other than this conditional one, it is not self-sufficient until "إمّا" occurs twice, as in His words ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِراً وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً﴾ and His words ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا رَأَوْاْ مَا يُوعَدُونَ إِمَّا ٱلعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ﴾. It is accusative only because "إمّا" is like "أوْ" (or) and governs nothing, as though He said "هَدَيْناهُ السبيلَ شاكراً أوْ كَفُورا" (We guided him on the way, grateful or ungrateful), making it accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and "حتى رَأَوْا ما يُوعَدُون العذابَ أَوْ الساعة" (until they see what they are promised, the punishment or the Hour), making it accusative as a badal (substitute).
The nominative is permissible after "إمّا" in everything in which a mubtadaʾ (subject) is permissible; [and]* if you said "مررت برجل إمّا قاعدٍ وإمّا قائمٍ" (I passed by a man either sitting or standing), it would be permissible. [Translator's note: the asterisk appears thus in the source.] What is in the Quran is also permissible [in this way], and it could be nominative, except that it has not been read so.
As for the one that does without repetition, it always has fatḥa on its alif, as in your saying "أَمّا عبد الله فمنطلق" (as for ʿAbd Allāh, he is leaving), and His words ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ [9] وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ﴾ and ﴿وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ﴾. Every "أمّا" that does not need to be repeated has fatḥa on its alif, except the one in conditionals.
"أَمّا" too governs nothing. Do you not see that you say ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ﴾, making it accusative by "تنهر", while "أمّا" has changed nothing in it?
The chapter on the genitive construct (iḍāfa) [with the first-person yāʾ].
As for His words ﴿فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, this yāʾ takes fatḥa in every case because the letter before it is vowelless, namely the alif in "هُدَى". So when you needed to vowel the yāʾ, you gave it fatḥa, because it is only vowelled with fatḥa. Similar to that are His words ﴿عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْهَا﴾. It is a dialect of the Arabs to say "عصَيَّ يا فَتى" (my staff, young man) and ﴿ هُدَيَّ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: since a vowelless letter preceded it and it was an alif, you turn it into yāʾ so that you assimilate it into the letter after it, and they make them run as one, which is lighter for them. As for His words ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾, ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ [and] ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾, [the yāʾ] was vowelled in the construct only because of the vowellessness of what precedes it, and the letter before it was made a yāʾ; He did not say "عَلايَ" or "لَدايَ", as you say "على زيد" and "لدى زيد", so as to distinguish it from nouns, because these are not nouns, whereas "عَصايَ", "هُدايَ" and "قَفايَ" (my nape) are nouns. Likewise ﴿أَفْتُونِي فِي رُؤْيَايَ﴾ and ﴿يٰبُشْرَايٰ هَـٰذَا غُلاَمٌ﴾, because the end of "بُشْرى" is vowelless.
Some read ﴿يا بُشْراي هذا غلام﴾ [Translator's note: the form as printed is the same as above; the reading meant is presumably "يا بُشْرى", without the possessive], not intending the construct, as you say "يا بشارة" (O good news).
When the letter [before the yāʾ] is not vowelless, you have the choice with the yāʾ: if you wish you make it vowelless, and if you wish you give it fatḥa, as in ﴿إِنِّيْۤ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ﴾ and ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ﴾, ﴿وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِيْ مُؤْمِناً﴾ and ﴿بَيْتِيَ﴾, [and] ﴿فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعَآئِيْۤ إِلاَّ فِرَاراً﴾ and ﴿دُعَآئِيۤ إِلاَّ﴾.
