Likewise, when an added alif and lām meet it, if you wish you drop the yāʾ because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and if you wish you give it fatḥa so that two vowelless letters do not come together; but the best of that is fatḥa, as in the words of Allah the Blessed and Exalted ﴿جَآءَنِيَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتُ مِن رَّبِّي﴾ and ﴿نِعْمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِي﴾ and the like; and that is how we read. If a connecting alif without lām meets it, you also have the choice in it, except that the best in this case is dropping [the yāʾ], and that is how we read: ﴿إِنِّي ٱصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ and ﴿ هَارُونَ أَخِي ٱشْدُدْ بِهِ أَزْرِي﴾.
When any of this is in the vocative, the yāʾ is dropped from it, as in ﴿يٰعِبَادِ فَٱتَّقُونِ﴾, ﴿رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ﴾ and ﴿رَّبِّ إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّي مَا يُوعَدُونَ﴾.
Some Arabs drop these yāʾs in the vocative and elsewhere, in everything. That is ugly and rare, except what is at the ends of verses (ruʾūs al-āy), where it is dropped in the pause, just as the Arabs drop [letters] from rhymes in their poetry, as in his saying [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the forty-fourth evidentiary verse]:
[أَبا مُنْذِرٍ أفنيتَ فاستبقِ بعضَنا] * حنانيكَ بعضُ الشرِّ أَهونُ من بَعْضِ
(Abū Mundhir, you have destroyed [us], so spare some of us; have mercy — some evil is lighter than other.)
and his saying [in the wāfir metre; this is the forty-fifth evidentiary verse]:
[ألا هُبِّي بِصَحْنِكِ فاصبَحينا] * وَلا تُبْقِي خُمورَ الأنْدَرينَ
(Ho, rise with your bowl and give us the morning draught, and do not spare the wines of al-Andarīn.)
[that is,] when they pause; when they connect, they say "من بعضِي" and "الأنْدرينا". [Translator's note: the source prints "من بعض" here; the sense requires the restored long vowel.] That is frequent at the ends of verses, as in His words ﴿بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِ﴾ [and] ﴿وَإِيَّايَ فَٱتَّقُونِ﴾: when they connect, they keep the yāʾ. Some people dropped the yāʾ both in pause and in connection, following that rare dialect; this is the reading of the generality [of readers], and that is how we read, because the written text follows it.
Some people paused with the yāʾ and connected with the yāʾ; that goes against the written text, because the written text has no yāʾ in it, though it is the good dialect form. We heard an eloquent Arab reciting [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the forty-sixth evidentiary verse]:
فما وَجَدَ النَّهْدِيُ وَجْداً وَجَدْتُهُ * ولا وَجَدَ العُذْرِيُّ قبلِ جَمِيلُ
(Neither the Nahdī felt a passion like the one I felt, nor the ʿUdhrī, Jamīl, before me.)
He means "قبلِي" (before me), and dropped the yāʾ. Some treated "قَبْل" as one treats what has no yāʾ, saying "قبلُ جميل" while meaning "قبلي", just as some Arabs said "يا ربُّ اغفِر لي" (O Lord, forgive me) with the nominative ending, meaning "يا ربّي" (O my Lord).
As for His words ﴿وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَاْ﴾ and ﴿أَضَلُّونَا ٱلسَّبِيلاْ﴾, the alif is kept in them because they are verse-endings; for some Arabs, namely the people of the Hijaz, make the ends of rhymes, when they pause on them, the same as when they connect them. All the Arabs, when they chant rhymes, keep yāʾ, wāw and alif at their ends.
As for His words ﴿يٰأَبَتِ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ﴾, He made this noun feminine with the hāʾ [i.e. tāʾ marbūṭa], as in your saying "رجُلٌ رَبْعَةٌ" (a man of middle height) and "غُلامٌ يَفَعَةٌ" (a youth near puberty); or He may have inserted it as compensation for what was removed from the noun. Some read it with fatḥa, as if they meant "يا أبتا" and dropped the alif just as they drop the yāʾ, as the poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the forty-first evidentiary verse]:
[ولست بمدرك ما فات مني] * "لهفَ" ولا بـ"ليتَ" ولا لَوَآني"
(I shall not recover what has escaped me by "alas", nor by "would that", nor by "if only I…")
He means "لَهْفاه" (alas!). What shows you that this noun was made feminine with the hāʾ is the poet's saying [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the forty-seventh evidentiary verse]:
تقولُ ابنتي لما رأتنِيَ شاحِباً * كأنَّكَ فينا يا أَبات غريبُ
(My daughter says, when she sees me pale: "Father, it is as though you were a stranger among us.")
He restored the alif and added the hāʾ to it, just as it was made feminine in his saying "يا أمتاه" (O mother!); so these are three letters. Some Arabs say "يا أمَّ لا تفعلي" (Mother, do not do it), shortening it (tarkhīm), as he said "يا صاحِ" (O companion). Some say "يا أميّ" and "يا أبي", in the dialect of those who say "يا غلامِي" (O my servant). And some say "يا أبِ" and "يا أمِّ", and this is the good one by analogy.

akhfash:83-83.t:
His saying ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾.
And His saying ﴿وَبِٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً﴾: He made it a command, as though He were saying "and goodness to parents", i.e. "do good, a doing of good".
And He said ﴿وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً﴾: it is on one of two aspects. Either "الحُسْنِ" is meant as "الحَسَنَ" (what is good), just as you say "البُخْل" and "البَخلَ" (miserliness); or He made "الحُسْنَ" (goodness) be "الحَسَنَ" by way of comparison, just as you say "إنَّما أَنْتَ أَكلٌ وشُرْبٌ" ("you are nothing but eating and drinking"). The poet said [in the wāfir metre; it is the hundred and eighth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
وَخَيْلٍ قدْ دَلَفْتٌ لَها بِخَيْلٍ * تَحِيَّةُ بَيْنِهِمْ ضَرْبٌ وَجِيعٌ
(Many a troop of horse I advanced against with horse, the greeting between them a painful blow.)
"دَلَفْتُ" means "I headed for"; and he made the greeting a blow. This word is not frequent in speech, but it has come in the Quran. Some of them read it ﴿حَسَنا﴾, meaning "say to them something good". And some of them said ﴿قولوا للناسِ حُسْنى﴾, making it feminine and not giving it tanwīn; and this hardly occurs, for "الحُسْنى" is only spoken with the alif and lām, just as its masculine is only spoken with the alif and lām. [So] if you said "جاءَني أَحْسَنُ وأَطْوَلُ" ("a better and a taller came to me"), it would not be good until you say "جاءَني الأَحْسَنُ والأَطْوَلُ" ("the better and the taller came to me"); and so with this, one says "جاءَتْنِي الحُسْنى والطُولى". Except that they have made some things of this kind nouns, such as "دُنْيا" (world) and "أُوْلَى". The rajaz poet said [it is the hundred and ninth shāhid]:
* في سَعْيِ دُنْيا طالَ ما قَدْ مَدَّتِ *
(In striving for a world that has long stretched [its span].)
And they say "هي خَيْرَةُ النِساءِ" ("she is the best of women") ["هنّ خَيْراتُ النِّساء"]; they hardly use it in the singular, though its singular use is permissible. And in the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فِيهِنَّ خَيْرَاتٌ حِسَانٌ﴾. That is because He did not intend [the pattern] "أَفْعَلَ" (elative); He only intended the feminine of "خير", because when one describes and says "فلانٌ خَيْرٌ" ("so-and-so is good"), it resembles the adjectives, so the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] was added for the feminine.
As for His saying ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾, then He said ﴿وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً﴾, then He said ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ﴾: it is because He addressed them after having spoken about them [in the third person]; and this is frequent in speech and poetry. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and tenth shāhid]:
أسيئي بِنا أوّ أَحْسِنِي لا مَلُومَةٌ * لَدَيْنا وَلا مَقْليةٌ إِنْ تَقَلَّبِ
(Treat us badly or treat us well — [you are] not blamed by us, nor hated, if [she] hates.)
They only mean "تَقَلَّيْتِ" ("you hated"). And the other said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and eleventh shāhid]:
شَطَّتْ مُزارَ العاشِقينَ فأصبحَتْ * عَسِراً عَلَيَّ طِلابُكِ ابْنَةٌ مَخْرَمِ
(She has gone far from the visiting-place of lovers, and seeking you, daughter of Makhram, has become hard for me.)
He only meant "and the daughter of Makhram became hard for me, the seeking of her". It is permissible to make the speech as though he addressed her, because when he said "she has gone far from the visiting-place of lovers", it is as though he said "you have gone far from the visiting-place of lovers", since it is she he means by this speech. Like it, of what departs from its beginning, is his saying [in the rajaz metre; it is the hundred and twelfth shāhid]:
* إنَّ تَميماً خُلِقَتْ مَلْمُوما *
(Tamīm was created compact.)
He meant the tribe by his saying "خُلِقَتْ" [feminine], then said "مَلْمُوما" [masculine] with reference to the clan or the man; and for that reason he said:
* مثلَ الصَّفا لا تَشْتَكِي الكُلُوما *
(Like the smooth rock, not complaining of wounds.)
Then he said:
* قَوماً تَرَى واحدَهُم صِهْمِيما *
(A people whose every one you see to be a fierce, unyielding man.)
So he brought the plural, because he meant the tribe or the clan. Then he said:
* لا راحِمَ الناسِ ولا مُرْحُوما *
(Neither showing mercy to people nor shown mercy.)
And the poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and thirteenth shāhid]:
أقولُ لَهُ والرمحُ يأطِرُمَتْنَهُ * تأَمَّل خُفافاً إِنَّنِي أَنَاذلِكا
(I say to him, while the spear bends his back: "Look well at Khufāf — I am that one.")
And [also recited] "تَبَيَّنْ خْفافاً"; he means "I am he". And in the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾: He spoke in the wording of the absent [third person] while it had been in address, because that indicates the meaning. And al-Aswad said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the hundred and fourteenth shāhid]:
وَجَفْنَةٍ كإِزاءِ الحَوْضُ مُتْرَعَةٍ * ترى جَوانِبَها بِالشَّحْمِ مَفْتُونا
(Many a huge bowl, like the spout of a trough, filled to the brim — you see its sides plastered with fat.)
This would be on [the basis] that he took it according to the meaning, i.e. you see every side of it; or he made the attribute of the plural singular, as in what has come in speech. And his saying "مأطِرُ مَتْنَه" [Translator's note: the verse has «يأطِرُ»] means it bends his back. Likewise ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾, then He said ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ﴾, because the one spoken about is the one addressed. Ruʾba said [in the rajaz metre; it is the hundred and fifteenth shāhid]:
الحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الاَعَزِّ الأَجْلَلِ * أَنْتَ مَلِيكُ الناسِ ربّاً فَاقْبَلِ
(Praise be to Allah, the Mightiest, the Most Majestic; You are the King of people, as Lord, so accept.)
And Zuhayr said [in the wāfir metre; it is the hundred and sixteenth shāhid]:
فإنّي لَوْ أُلاقِيكَ أجْتَهَدْنَا * وكانَ لِكُلِّ مُنْكَرَةٍ كِفاء
فأُبْرِىءَ مُوضَحاتِ الرأسِ مِنْهُ * وَقَدْ يَشْفِى من الجَرَبِ الهِناءُ
(If I were to meet you, we would strive [against each other], and every outrage would have its match; and I would heal the head-wounds [I gave] from him [Translator's note: the shift from "you" to "him" is the point of the citation] — and tar sometimes cures mange.)
And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿ذُوقُواْ فِتْنَتَكُمْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾: He used the masculine after the feminine, as though He meant "this is the matter which you used to seek to hasten". Like it is ﴿فَلَماَّ رَأَى ٱلشَّمْسَ بَازِغَةً قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَبِّي هَـٰذَآ أَكْبَرُ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَتْ﴾: this would be on [the basis of] "what I see is my lord", i.e. this thing is my lord. And this resembles what the commentators said on ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمْ﴾: he said: "إلى" only came in because the meaning of "الرَفَث" (sexual approach) and "الأفْضاء" (going in to) is one, so it is as though He said "going in to your wives"; and one only says "رَفْثَ بامرَأَتِه", and one does not say "إلى امرأته". In my view this is like what is permissible of the "باء" in place of "إلى" in [His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بَيۤ إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي مِنَ ٱلسِّجْنِ﴾, which is only "أحسن اليّ" ("He was good to me"), so He did not [use] "إلى" and put the "باء" in its place], and in place of "على" in His saying ﴿فَأَثَابَكُمْ غَمَّاً بِغَمٍّ﴾, which is only "distress upon distress", [and His saying] ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِن تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ﴾, i.e. "with [lit. upon] a heap of gold", just as you say "مررتُ بِهِ" and "مررت عَلَيْهِ" ("I passed by him"), and as the poet said — and one whom I trust told me that he heard it from the Arabs — [in the wāfir metre; it is the twenty-fourth shāhid]:
[Translator's note: "twenty-fourth" is as written; it does not fit the surrounding sequence.]
إذا رَضِيَتْ عَلَيَّ بَنُو قُشَيْرٍ * لَعَمْرُ اللّهِ أَعْجَبَنِي رِضاها
(When the Banū Qushayr are pleased with me — by the life of Allah — their pleasure delights me.)
He means "عنى" [Translator's note: printed thus; i.e. «عنّي», "with me"]. And this resembles ﴿وَإِذَا خَلَوْاْ إِلَىٰ شَيَاطِينِهِمْ﴾, because you say "خَلَوْتُ إلَيْهِ وصنعنا كذا وكذا" ("I was alone with him and we did such-and-such") and "خَلَوْتُ به". And if you wish, you may take it in the meaning of His saying ﴿مَنْ أَنصَارِيۤ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. "with Allah", and as He said ﴿وَنَصَرْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ﴾, i.e. "against the people".

akhfash:84-84.t:
[And His saying] ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ لاَ تَسْفِكُونَ دِمَآءَكُمْ﴾: this is nominative because every verb of the forms "يَفْعَلُ هو", "تَفْعَل أنت", "أَفْعلٌ أَنا" and "نَفْعَلُ نَحن" [i.e. the imperfect] is always nominative (marfūʿ), and nothing governs it except the particles I mentioned to you: the particles of the accusative, or the particles of the jussive, command, prohibition and condition. None of these is here; it is only nominative because of its occurring in the position of nouns. The meaning of this speech is reported speech (ḥikāya), as though He said "We made them swear: they will not worship", i.e. We said to them: "By Allah, you will not worship"; that is because it is read ﴿يَعْبُدون﴾ and ﴿تَعْبُدون﴾. He said ﴿وَحِفْظاً مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَّارِدٍ﴾ ﴿لاَّ يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَلإِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ وَيُقْذَفُونَ﴾: if you wish, you may make "لا يَسَّمَّعُون" a new beginning (mubtadaʾ clause); and if you wish, you may say: it has the meaning of "أنْ لا لا يَسَّمَّعُوا" [Translator's note: «لا» is printed twice] — so when "أنْ" was dropped, it became nominative, just as you say "أَتَيْتُكَ تُعْطِيني وتُحْسِنُ إِلَيَّ وتَنْظُرُ في حاجتي" ("I came to you [so that] you give me, treat me well and see to my need"). Like it is "مُرْهُ يُعطِيني" ("order him [to] give me"): if you wish, you take it as "and he will give me", and if you wish, as "that he give me"; so when you dropped "أَنْ", it became nominative. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and seventh shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
أ‌لا أَيُّهذا الزاجِرِي احضر الوغي‌ * وأَنْ أَتْبَعَ اللَّذَّاتِ هَلْ انت مُخْلِدِي
(O you who chide me for being present at battle and for pursuing pleasures — can you make me immortal?)
So "أَحْضُرَ" has the meaning of "أَنْ أُحْضُرَ" ("that I be present").

akhfash:85-85.t:
He said ﴿تَظَاهَرُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِٱلإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ﴾: he took it from "تَتَظاهَرُونَ" and assimilated the tāʾ into the ẓāʾ, and that is how we read. It has also been read ﴿تَظاهَرون﴾, light, by dropping the second tāʾ, because it is added without [contributing] a meaning. And He said ﴿وَإِن يَأتُوكُمْ أَسْرىٰ﴾, and it has been read ﴿أُسَارَى﴾. That is because "أَسير" (captive) is [of the pattern] "فَعِيل", and it resembles "مَرِيضاً" (sick), because there is an affliction in him as there is in the sick person, and this is a "فَعِيل" like it; and they said for the plural of "المريض", "مَرْضى". And they said ﴿أُسارَى﴾, making it like "سكارَى" (drunk) and "كُسالىَ" (lazy), because the plural of "فَعْلان" that denotes an affliction may share with the plural of "فَعِيل" and the plural of "فَعِل", as in "حَبِطٌ", "حَبْطى" and "حُباطَى", and "حَبِجٌ", "حَبْجى" and "حُباجى" [both: having a swollen belly]. And they said ﴿أَسارى﴾, as they said ﴿سَكَارَىٰ﴾.
Some of them said ﴿تَفْدُوهم﴾, from "تَفْدِى", and some of them ﴿تُفادُوهم﴾, from "فادَى", "يُفادِي", and that is how we read; and all of that is correct.
And He said ﴿فَمَا جَزَآءُ مَن يَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ مِنكُمْ إِلاَّ خِزْيٌ﴾, and He said ﴿مَا هَـٰذَا إِلاَّ بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ﴾ and ﴿وَمَآ أَمْرُنَآ إِلاَّ وَاحِدَةٌ﴾, in the nominative, because every khabar (predicate) of "ما" in which the bāʾ is not good is nominative, since "ما" is not likened to the verb in that position; it is only likened to the verb in the position where the bāʾ is good, because then it has the meaning of "ليس" with nothing sharing it. That is the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿مَا هَـٰذَا بَشَراً﴾. And Tamīm put it in the nominative, because it is not of their dialect to liken "ما" to the verb.
And He said ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾, and in another place ﴿هَا أَنْتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾, like some of what we have mentioned, and it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs; the [particle of] attention (tanbīh) is repeated for emphasis. And you say "ها أَنَا هذا" ("here I am, this one") and "ها أَنْتَ هذا", making "هذا" refer to the one addressed; and you say "هذا أنت". Something stronger than this has come. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said ﴿مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوءُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلْقُوَّةِ﴾, while it is the band that is weighed down by the keys. He said [it is the hundred and seventeenth shāhid (evidentiary verse), in the majzūʾ al-wāfir metre]:
تَنُوءُ بِها فَتُثْقِلُها * عَجِيزَتُها......
(Her buttocks weigh her down, and burden her …)
He means "she is weighed down by her buttocks", i.e. she does not rise except with effort after effort. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the hundred and eighteenth shāhid]:
مِثْلُ القَنافِذِ هَدَّاجُونَ قَدْ بَلَغَت * نَجْرانَ أَوْ بَلَغَتْ سَوآتِهِم هَجَرُ
(Like hedgehogs, creeping about by night — [their foul deeds] have reached Najrān, or Hajar has reached their foul deeds [i.e. as worded, with the roles reversed].)
He means that the foul deeds reached Hajar; and "هَجَرُ" is nominative because the ode rhymes in the nominative. Like this is the saying of the poet [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and nineteenth shāhid]:
وَتَلْحَقُ خَيْلٌ لا هَوادَةَ بَينَها * وتَشْقى الرِّماحُ بالضَياطِرةُ الحُمْرِ
(And horsemen with no truce between them overtake [one another], and the spears are made wretched by the red, bulky men.)
While it is the bulky men who are made wretched by the spears. "الضياطرةُ" are the bulky ones; their singular is "ضَيْطار", like "بَيْطار" (farrier). And like the saying of the poet [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and twentieth shāhid]:
لَقَدْ خِفْتُ حَتَّى ما تزَيدُ مَخافَتِي * عَلى وعِلٍ بِذِي الفَقارَةِ عاقِلِ
(I have feared until my fear does not exceed [that of] a mountain goat taking refuge at Dhū al-Faqāra.)
He means: until the fear of a mountain goat does not exceed my fear.

akhfash:88-88.t:
He said ﴿فَقَلِيلاً مَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, and its interpretation is "so little do they believe"; "ما" is redundant (zāʾida), as He said ﴿فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ﴾, saying "so by mercy from Allah"; and He said ﴿إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ﴾, i.e. "it is surely true, just as you speak". The addition of "ما" in the Quran and in speech in this way is frequent. He said [in the munsariḥ metre; it is the hundred and twenty-first shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
‌لَوْ بَأَبانَيْنِ جاءَ يَخْطِبُها * خُضِّبَ ما أَنْفُ خاطِبٍ بِدَمِ
(Had he come to ask for her hand at Abānān, the nose of a suitor would have been dyed with blood.)
I.e. the nose of a suitor would have been dyed with blood.

akhfash:89-89.t:
He said ﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ وَكَانُواْ مِن قَبْلُ يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ مَّا عَرَفُواْ كَفَرُواْ بِهِ﴾. If it is said, "Where then is the answer to ﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ﴾?", I say: "Its [kind of] answer is frequent in the Quran, [and] it was dispensed with in this place since its meaning was known." Likewise in all speech, when it grows long, things come in it that have no answers in that place, and the meaning suffices without it, as in the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بَل للَّهِ ٱلأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً﴾: they mention [that] its interpretation is "if mountains were moved by a Quran other than this, this Quran would be one by which mountains are moved"; so the wording of the answer was dispensed with since the meaning was known. And He said ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوْاْ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحْمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُواْ فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفَازَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾, and no answer [i.e. second object] came for the first "تحسَبَنَّ"; it was left out, being dispensed with by the answers in the Quran. And He said ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ هُوَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ﴾, whose meaning is "let them not think it good for them"; that speech was omitted, and in what remained there was an indication of the meaning. Like it is ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّقُواْ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾, then He said ﴿وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ﴾ before bringing His saying "they did such-and-such", because that is frequent in the Quran, and it was dispensed with by it. And in His saying ﴿وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ مِّنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلاَّ كَانُواْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ there was an indication that they turned away, so this sufficed; and likewise everything in which the like of this is permissible. And He said ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلآخِرَةِ لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ وَلِيَدْخُلُواْ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُواْ مَا عَلَوْاْ تَتْبِيراً﴾, and He said ﴿لِيُتَبَرِّواْ﴾ with the meaning "We left them and you alone; We did not protect you from them, because of your sins". And He said ﴿لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ without mentioning that He left them and you alone, by way of abandonment in the state of trial for what they had previously done, and then did not prevent their enemies from being given power over them because of their wrongdoing. And He said ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَىۤ إِذِ ٱلظَّالِمُونَ فِي غَمَرَاتِ ٱلْمَوْتِ﴾, and there is no answer to this. And He said ﴿وَلَوْ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوۤاْ إِذْ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْعَذَابَ﴾, and the answer to this is only in the meaning; and this is frequent. We will explain everything we come across, if Allah wills. And they have claimed that this verse has no answer [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and twenty-second shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
وَدَوِّيَّةٍ قَفْرٍ تَمَشّى نَعامُها * كَمَشْيِ النَّصارى في خِفافِ الأَرَنْدَجِ
(And many a barren desert, whose ostriches walk like Christians walking in boots of black leather.)
He means "and many a desert", and then he did not bring an answer for it. And he said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the hundred and twenty-third shāhid]:
حتَى إذا أسْلَكُوهُ في قُتائِدَةٍ * شَلاًّ كَما تَطْرُدُ الجَمالَةُ الشرُدُا
(Until, when they had driven them into [the pass of] Qutāʾida, driving hard, as camel-drivers drive the strays …)
This has no answer except in the meaning. And some of them claimed regarding this verse [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and fifth shāhid]:
فإذا وذلِكَ يا كُبَيْشَةُ لَمْ يكنْ * إلاّ كَلَمَّةِ حالِمٍ بِخِيالِ
(And then that, O Kubaysha, was nothing but like a dreamer's brief visit from a phantom.)
They said: the wāw in it is not redundant; rather, the khabar (predicate) is implied.

akhfash:90-90.t: He said ﴿بِئْسَمَا ٱشْتَرَوْاْ بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ أَن يَكْفُرُواْ بِمَآ أنَزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بَغْياً أَن يُنَزِّلُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾: ﴿ما﴾ by itself is a noun, and ﴿أَن يَكْفُرُواْ﴾ is an explanation of it, as in "نِعْمَ رَجُلاً زَيْدٌ" ("what an excellent man Zayd is"); and ﴿أَنْ يُنَزِّل﴾ is a badal (substitute) for ﴿بِمَآ أنَزَلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.

akhfash:91-91.t:
He said ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ مُصَدِّقاً لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ قُلْ فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْبِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He put ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ in the accusative because it is a khabar (predicate) [following] a definite [noun] [i.e. a ḥāl (circumstantial)]. And ﴿تَقْتُلُونَ﴾ has the meaning of "you killed", as the poet said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and twenty-fourth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
وَلَقَدْ أمرُّ على اللَّئِيمِ يَسُبُّني * فَمَضَيْتُ ثُمَّتَ قُلتُ لا يَعْنِيني
(I pass by the base man who insults me, and I went on, then said: "He does not concern me".)
By his saying "أَمُرُّ" ("I pass") he means "I passed".

akhfash:96-96.t: His saying ﴿وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَ﴾ is like "ما زَيْدٌ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ أنْ يُعَمَّرَ" ("Zayd — his being given long life will not remove him") and "ما زَيْدٌ بِضارِّهِ أَنْ يقُومَ" ("Zayd — his standing will not harm him"). [So "أنْ يُعَمَّرَ"] is in the position of the nominative, and the bāʾ is good [here], just as you say "ما عبدُ الله بملازِمِهِ زَيْدٌ" ("ʿAbd Allāh — Zayd is not keeping close to him").

akhfash:97-97.t:
His saying ﴿مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً لِّجِبْرِيلَ﴾: among the Arabs are those who say ﴿لِجِبرئِيلَ﴾; they use the hamza and they do not use it. Likewise ﴿إسرائيل﴾: some of them use the hamza and some do not. And they say ﴿مِيكائِيل﴾, using the hamza and not using it, and they say ﴿مِيكال﴾, just as they said ﴿جِبْرِيل﴾. Some of them said ﴿جبرعَل﴾, and I do not know [its rationale], except that I have heard ﴿إِسرائِل﴾. And some of them said ﴿إسْرِييلِ﴾, inclining (imāla) the rāʾ. Abū al-Ḥasan said: "In 'Jibrīl' there are six dialectal forms: جَبْراييل, جَبْرَئيل, جَبْرئِلْ
جَبْراعيل جَبْرَعِيل جَبرعل
and جَبْريل and جِبريلَ
فَعليل فِعليل
and جَبْرائِل.
جبراعل.
[Translator's note: the list is laid out as in the source, with what appear to be pattern equivalents (using ع as a stand-in for the hamza, and the measures فَعليل / فِعليل) on separate lines; more than six forms appear.]

akhfash:98-98.t:
He said ﴿مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً للَّهِ وَمَلاۤئِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِّلْكَافِرِينَ﴾: He made the noun overt [instead of a pronoun] although He had mentioned it at the beginning of the speech. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and twenty-fifth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
ليتَ الغُرابَ غَداةَ يَنْعَبُ دَائِباً * كانَ الغُرابُ مُقَطَّعَ الأوْداجِ
(Would that the crow, on the morning it croaks incessantly — that the crow had its jugular veins cut.)

akhfash:100-100.t: He said ﴿أَوَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُواْ عَهْداً﴾: this is a wāw placed together with the interrogative particle, and it is like the fāʾ in His saying ﴿أَفَكُلَّمَا جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لاَ تَهْوَىٰ أَنْفُسُكُمْ﴾. This is frequent in the Quran and in speech, and both are redundant (zāʾida) on this view. It is like the fāʾ in your saying "أَفَا الله لَتَصْنَعَنَّ كَذَا وكَذا" ("by Allah, you will surely do such-and-such!") and your saying to a man "أَفَلا تَقُوم" ("will you not stand?"). And if you wish, you may make the fāʾ and the wāw here a conjunction.

akhfash:102-102.t:
His saying ﴿وَمَآ أُنْزِلَ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ﴾: they [هاروت and ماروت] are maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿ٱلْمَلَكَيْنِ﴾, or a badal (substitute) for them; but they are foreign, so they are diptotes, and their position is genitive. And ﴿بابلَ﴾ is a diptote because of its femininity. That is because the name of every feminine [entity] of two letters, or of three letters with the middle one quiescent, is fully declinable; and whatever feminine [name] is other than that is a diptote as long as it is the name of a feminine [entity].
And He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَقُولاَ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلاَ تَكْفُرْ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا﴾: His saying ﴿فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ﴾ is not an answer to His saying ﴿فَلاَ تَكْفُرْ﴾; it is only a new beginning (mubtadaʾ), then He conjoined [something] to it and said ﴿وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلاَ يَنفَعُهُمْ﴾. And He said ﴿يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ﴾, because each of them is a "زوج" (spouse): the woman is a زوج and the man is a زوج. He said ﴿وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾, and He said ﴿مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾. And "هُما زَوْجٌ" ("they are a pair") is also said of two, just as you say "هُما سَواءٌ" and "هُما سِيّانِ" ("they are alike"). [And "الزَوْج" is also the patterned cloth thrown over the camel-litter.] The poet said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and twenty-sixth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
مِنْ كُلِّ مَحْفُوفٍ يظُلُّ غِصيَّةُ * زَوْجٌ عَلَيهِ كِلَّةٌ وَقِرامُها
([Women] in every covered litter, whose frame is shaded by a patterned cloth, with a canopy over it and its curtain.)
And they have said "الزَوْجَة" (wife). The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the hundred and twenty-seventh shāhid]:
زَوْجَةُ أَشْمَطَ مَرْهُوبٍ بَوادِرُهُ * قَدْ صارَ في رَأْسِهِ التَخْويصُ والنزَعُ
(The wife of a grizzled man whose outbursts are feared, on whose head greying and receding hair have appeared.)
And He said ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُواْ لَمَنِ ٱشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلاَقٍ﴾: this is the lām of ibtidāʾ (the inceptive lām), which enters after [verbs of] knowing and the like, and a new clause begins after it. You say "لَقَدْ علمت لَزَيدٌ خيرٌ منك" ("I knew that Zayd is indeed better than you"). He said ﴿لَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾, and He said ﴿لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰ أَبِينَا مِنَّا﴾.
And He said ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُواْ لَمَنِ ٱشْتَرَاهُ﴾, then He said ﴿لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: by the first He means the devils, because they had known; and [by] ﴿ولَّوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ He means humans. And in His saying ﴿لَمَثُوبَةٌ﴾ there was an indication of "they would have been rewarded", so the answer was dispensed with by it.

akhfash:103-103.t: He said ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُواْ وٱتَّقَوْا لَمَثُوبَةٌ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ﴾: His saying ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُواْ وٱتَّقَوْا﴾ has no answer in the wording, but [it has one] in the meaning: He means "they would have been rewarded". His saying ﴿لَمَثَوبَةٌ﴾ indicates "they would have been rewarded", so the answer was dispensed with by it. And in His saying ﴿لَمَثُوبَةٌ﴾ this lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (the inceptive lām), as I explained to you.

akhfash:105-105.t: He said ﴿مَّا يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَلاَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾, i.e. "nor of the idolaters" — they do not wish ﴿أَن يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.

akhfash:106-106.t: He said ﴿مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِّنْهَا أَوْ مِثْلِهَا﴾, and some of them said ﴿نَنْسَأْها﴾, i.e. "We postpone it". It is like ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيۤءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾, because it is postponement. [And] "النَسِيئَةُ" (deferment of payment) and "النَسِيءُ" have one origin, from "أنسأت", except that you say "أَنْسَأتُ الشَيْءَ", i.e. I postponed the thing, and its maṣdar (verbal noun) is "النَسِيءُ"; and "أَنْسَأْتُكَ الدَيْنَ", i.e. I let you postpone the debt. It is as though he said "أَنْسَأْتُكَ" so "نَسَأْتُ". And "النَسِيء" is that they used to insert a month into a month. And some of them said ﴿أَوْ نَنْسَها﴾; all of that is correct. It is jussive by the condition. And al-nasīʾ with respect to the month is postponement.

akhfash:108-108.t: He said ﴿أَمْ تُرِيدُونَ أَن تَسْأَلُواْ رَسُولَكُمْ كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ﴾; and whoever lightens [the hamza] says ﴿سُيِل﴾. If it is said: "How did you make it 'between-between' (bayna bayna), when it would be between a quiescent yāʾ and the hamza, and a quiescent yāʾ does not come after a ḍamma, while the sīn has a ḍamma?", I say: "As for [the pattern] 'فُعِلَ', a quiescent yāʾ may come after a ḍamma, because they have said 'قُيْل' and 'بُيْعَ'. And the yāʾ in some [forms of] 'فُعِلَ' may become a pure wāw because of the ḍamma before it, being with it in one word, just as you say 'لم تَوْطُؤ الدابَّةُ' and as you say 'قَدْ رُؤِس فلان' ('so-and-so has been made chief')."

akhfash:111-111.t: He said ﴿لَن يَدْخُلَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ إِلاَّ مَن كَانَ هُوداً أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ﴾: they claimed that "الهُود" is the plural of "الهائِد", and "الهائد" is the penitent who returns to the truth. And He said in another place ﴿وَقَالُواْ كُونُواْ هُوداً﴾, i.e. be returners to the truth. [And one says] "هائِد" and "هُوَّد", like "ناقِه" [and "نُقَّه" (convalescent), and] "عائِدْ" and "عُوَّد", "حائِل" and "حُوَّل", and "بازِل" and "بُزَّل". He made ﴿مَن كَانَ﴾ singular because the wording of ﴿مَنْ﴾ is singular, and He used the plural in His saying ﴿هُوداً أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ﴾. On this aspect you say "مَنْ كانَ صاحبك" ("whoever were your companion[s]").

akhfash:114-114.t:
He said ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ مَّنَعَ مَسَاجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُ﴾: it is only "from His name being mentioned in them", but prepositions are frequently dropped with "أَنْ", and what precedes governs it, so that it is in the position of the accusative [i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition]. Or ﴿أَن يُذْكَرَ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for "المَساجِد"; they mean: "who is more unjust than one who prevented [His name] being mentioned".
And He said ﴿وَسَعَىٰ فِي خَرَابِهَآ﴾: this is on [the pattern of] "مَنَعَ" and "سَعَى" [i.e. singular verbs, following the wording of «مَنْ»]; then He said ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ إِلاَّ خَآئِفِينَ﴾, making it plural, because ﴿مَنْ﴾ may have the meaning of a group.

akhfash:115-115.t: He said ﴿فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّواْ فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ ٱللَّهِ﴾, because ﴿أَيْنَما﴾ is one of the jussive particles of the condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is in the fāʾ.

akhfash:117-117.t:
He said ﴿وَإِذَا قَضَىٰ أَمْراً فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: He put it in the nominative by conjunction, as though He only meant to say "He only says 'Be', and it is". Its nominative may also be on the basis of ibtidāʾ (a new beginning). And He said ﴿إِذَآ أَرَدْنَاهُ أَن نَّقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: if you make ﴿يَكُون﴾ here conjoined, you put it in the accusative, because ﴿أَنْ نَقُولَ﴾ is accusative by "أَنْ", as though He meant ﴿أَنْ نَقُولَ﴾ ﴿فيكونَ﴾. If he says: "How so, when the fāʾ is not in this meaning?", [the answer is that] the fāʾ and the wāw may conjoin to what precedes them and what follows them even if it is not in its meaning, as in "ما أنتَ وزيداً" ("what have you to do with Zayd?"), while he only means "you did not strike Zayd" [Translator's note: translated as written]; and you put it in the nominative on [the basis of] "what are you, and what is Zayd?", though that is not its meaning. And like your saying "إيّاكَ والأَسَدَ" ("beware of the lion"). The nominative in His saying ﴿فيَكُونُ﴾ is on the basis of ibtidāʾ, as in His saying ﴿لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي ٱلأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ﴾; and He said ﴿لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّخِذَهَا هُزُواً﴾. The accusative is also possible in His saying ﴿ويَتَّخَذَها﴾ and in ﴿نُقِرَّ في الأرْحامِ﴾, [conjoined] to the beginning of the speech. The poet said, using the nominative on the basis of ibtidāʾ [in the wāfir metre; it is the hundred and twenty-eighth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
‌‌يُعالِجُ عاقِراً أَعْيَتْ عَلَيْهِ * لِيَلْقِحَها فَيَنْتِجُها حُوارا
(He works on a barren [she-camel] who has defeated him, to impregnate her, and then she bears him a young camel.)
And the poet also said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and twenty-ninth shāhid]:
وما هُوَ إلاّ أَنَّ أَراها فُجاءَةً * فَأَبْهَتُ حَتَّى ما أَكَادُ أُجِيبُ
(It is nothing but that I see her suddenly, and I am struck dumb, so that I can hardly reply.)
The accusative in his saying ﴿فأَبْهَتُ﴾ is by conjunction, and the nominative is on the basis of ibtidāʾ.
